title: Blunt Thoracic Aortic Injury in the Geriatric Population: Results from the Aortic Trauma Foundation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The management of blunt thoracic aortic injury (BTAI) is evolving as the trauma population ages, yet the impact of age on treatment patterns and outcomes remains incompletely defined. STUDY DESIGN: A retrospective analysis of the Aortic Trauma Foundation registry (November 2016 to November 2023) identified 823 patients with BTAI, including 118 geriatric patients (65 years and older). Demographics, injury characteristics, management strategies, and outcomes were compared between the geriatric and younger (younger than 65 years) cohorts. RESULTS: Geriatric patients more frequently presented after falls (17.8% vs 6.7%, p < 0.0001) and had a higher proportion of grade IV injuries (18.5% vs 9.2%, p = 0.0021), with no difference in admission systolic blood pressure (116 vs 116, p = 0.960) or Injury Severity Score (31 vs 33, p = 0.150). Management strategies were similar between groups, including nonoperative (37.3% vs 36.9%, p = 0.932), open (4.2% vs 1.9%, p = 0.132), and endovascular repair (58.5% vs 61.1%, p = 0.584). Despite comparable treatment approaches, geriatric patients had higher in-hospital mortality (27.1% vs 10.9%, p < 0.0001) and aortic-related mortality (8.5% vs 3.4%, p = 0.010). CONCLUSIONS: Geriatric patients with BTAI sustain more severe injuries and experience significantly higher mortality despite similar management strategies. These findings suggest that current treatment paradigms may not adequately address age-associated risk and highlight the need for age-specific management considerations.

title: Percutaneous Renal Denervation for Resistant Hypertension in a High-Risk Real-World Population: Preliminary Results From a Prospective Single-Center Experience.
abstract: Renal denervation (RDN) is an adjunctive treatment for selected patients with resistant hypertension. We report the preliminary effectiveness and safety of radiofrequency RDN in a high-risk real-world population. This prospective, observational, single-center study enrolled 18 patients who underwent bilateral RDN using the Symplicity Spyral system. All had baseline office systolic BP (SBP) > 155 mmHg and diastolic BP > 90 mmHg despite at least three antihypertensive drugs at the maximum tolerated doses. Clinical response required both an office SBP reduction ≥ 10 mm Hg and a mean 24-h ambulatory SBP reduction ≥ 5 mm Hg. Outcomes were assessed within 72 h and at 1 month. All procedures were technically successful. At 72 h, 15 patients (83.3%) met both response criteria; all had an office SBP reduction ≥ 20 mm Hg. At 1 month, 16 (88.9%) were responders and 2 (11.1%) were nonresponders. Among responders, five discontinued one drug and continued dual therapy, whereas 11 continued three drugs at reduced doses. Procedural events included one iatrogenic renal artery dissection, one femoral artery dissection with perforation, one guidewire fracture successfully retrieved with an endovascular snare, and two femoral hematomas. Renal function did not deteriorate. In conclusion, radiofrequency RDN was technically feasible and was followed by an early clinical response in most patients. The small sample, short follow-up, and absence of a control group preclude definitive efficacy conclusions.
englishSummary: Renal denervation (RDN) is an adjunctive treatment for selected patients with resistant hypertension. We report the preliminary effectiveness and safety of radiofrequency RDN in a high-risk real-world population. This prospective, observational, single-center study enrolled 18 patients who underwent bilateral RDN using the Symplicity Spyral system.

title: Identification of perioperative risk factors for retrograde type A dissection after thoracic endovascular aortic repair for type B dissection.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To identify risk factors and develop a predictive model for retrograde type A dissection (RTAD) following thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) for type B aortic dissection (TBAD). METHODS: We analyzed TBAD patients who underwent TEVAR from 2014 to 2024 (IRB:No. TJ-IRB20230805). Patients developing RTAD within 1 year were matched with controls by age, sex, operation date, and location. Logistic regression identified risk factors, and a nomogram was constructed. Model performance was assessed using ROC curves. RESULTS: p p p p p p Of 2383 patients, 76 (3.19%) developed RTAD within one year. 65 RTAD cases and 195 matched controls were analyzed. RTAD patients had a greater horizontal distance of the ascending aorta (HDAA) than controls (53.34 mm vs. 43.05 mm, < .001). Multivariate analysis identified younger age (OR = 0.95, = .008), larger HDAA (OR = 1.14, < .001), aortic root dilatation (OR = 2.85, = .006), shorter stent length (OR = 0.99, = .029), and absence of postoperative bradycardic drug use (OR = 0.31, = .005) as independent RTAD risk factors. The model showed good discrimination (AUC = 0.85). CONCLUSION: Younger age, larger HDAA, aortic root dilatation, shorter stent length, and no bradycardic drugs postoperatively are independent predictors of RTAD after TEVAR. For TBAD patients with a high risk of RTAD, clinicians should consider the possibility of having connective tissue diseases, select stents appropriately, and optimize postoperative treatment with strict follow-up.

METHODS: We analyzed TBAD patients who underwent TEVAR from 2014 to 2024 (IRB:No. TJ-IRB20230805).

title: Efficacy and Safety of Intraosseous Regional Versus Intravenous Tranexamic Acid in Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Tranexamic acid (TXA) reduces perioperative blood loss in total knee arthroplasty (TKA); however, evidence for intraosseous regional administration (IORA) remains limited. We evaluated the efficacy and safety of IORA-TXA versus intravenous TXA (IV-TXA) in TKA. METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, single-center trial, 98 patients undergoing primary TKA were randomized 1:1 to IORA-TXA or IV-TXA (49 per group) at a uniform dose of 20 mg/kg. The primary outcome was calculated perioperative blood loss. Secondary efficacy outcomes included calculated hidden blood loss, postoperative hemoglobin (Hb) levels, and transfusion rate. Safety outcomes included deep vein thrombosis (DVT), muscular calf vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism (PE), and wound-related complications. RESULTS: Compared with IV-TXA, IORA-TXA reduced calculated perioperative blood loss (674.8 ± 335.0 vs. 817.5 ± 357.2 mL; mean difference, 142.6 mL; 95% CI, 7.4-277.8; p = 0.038) and calculated hidden blood loss (644.8 ± 335.5 vs. 790.9 ± 339.0 mL; mean difference, 146.1 mL; 95% CI, 10.9-281.3; p = 0.035). Postoperative Hb was similar on POD1 (134.0 ± 9.8 vs. 130.1 ± 11.1 g/L; p = 0.067) but was higher with IORA-TXA on POD2 (119.8 ± 8.3 vs. 113.8 ± 11.5 g/L; mean difference 6.0 g/L; 95% CI 2.0-10.0; p = 0.005) and POD3 (114.8 ± 7.9 vs. 109.8 ± 12.6 g/L; mean difference 5.0 g/L; 95% CI 0.8-9.2; p = 0.020). No patient required blood transfusion. DVT detected by routine postoperative Doppler occurred numerically more often with IORA-TXA than with IV-TXA: 10.2% (95% CI, 3.4%-22.2%) versus 0.0% (95% CI, 0.0%-7.3%); p = 0.056. CONCLUSIONS: IORA-TXA reduced calculated perioperative and hidden blood loss and improved early postoperative Hb preservation compared with IV-TXA. However, DVT incidence was numerically higher with IORA-TXA, indicating a potential thromboembolic safety signal that warrants confirmation in larger, adequately powered trials. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Therapeutic Level I. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

title: Implementation of a multi-disciplinary hemodialysis access clinic improves time to surgical evaluation and access case volume.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Delays in hemodialysis access creation contribute to prolonged tunneled dialysis catheter dependence and morbidity. In March 2025, our institution implemented a multidisciplinary accelerated hemodialysis access clinic with weekly reserved appointments, same-day duplex vein mapping, and streamlined nephrology-to-surgery referral. We evaluated its effect on access volume, timing to surgical evaluation, and catheter dependence. METHODS: We performed a retrospective chart review of adults undergoing hemodialysis access procedures at a tertiary academic center from March 17, 2024 to March 13, 2026. Access volume was compared before and after implementation. Patient-level timing metrics were compared between patients evaluated in standard vascular surgery clinic versus multidisciplinary accelerated clinic. RESULTS: p p p p p p Mean monthly access volume increased from 3.08 ± 2.15 to 8.58 ± 3.00 cases after implementation, an increase of 5.5 cases per month ( < 0.001). Annual access volume increased from 37 to 103 cases ( < 0.001). Among 53 patients, 29 were evaluated in the standard clinic and 24 in the multidisciplinary clinic. Referral-to-clinic time decreased from 63.6 ± 47.7 to 41.0 ± 35.9 days ( = 0.01). Clinic-to-operation time did not differ significantly (21.8 ± 18.5 vs 27.1 ± 17.2 days; = 0.14). Overall referral-to-operation time decreased from 85.4 ± 51.5 to 68.2 ± 43.9 days but did not reach significance ( = 0.07). Catheter dependence was lower in the multidisciplinary cohort (29% vs 48%; OR 0.36, 95% CI 0.11-1.16). Same-day vein mapping was performed more frequently in the accelerated clinic cohort than in the standard clinic cohort (100% vs 51.7%, < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: A multidisciplinary accelerated hemodialysis access clinic increased procedural volume and shortened time to surgical evaluation. However, total time to access creation was not significantly reduced, suggesting that downstream operative capacity may remain an important barrier.

title: Comparison of arteriovenous fistula patency in lipoprotein apheresis and haemodialysis: A matched case-control study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Arteriovenous fistulas constitute an effective vascular access option for haemodialysis, demonstrating high patency rates and lower infection risk compared with synthetic accesses. Treatment algorithms and patient characteristics differ between haemodialysis and apheresis therapy, and fistula outcomes in patients receiving lipoprotein apheresis have not yet been systematically evaluated. METHODS: This single-centre, retrospective cohort study compared arteriovenous fistula outcomes in 29 patients receiving lipoprotein apheresis with those of 87 frequency-matched patients on haemodialysis. Matching criteria included age, sex, fistula configuration and diabetes mellitus status. Primary and secondary patency rates and associated risk factors were assessed over a 24-month follow-up period using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analysis. RESULTS: n n n n p p p p The study included patients with radiocephalic ( = 72) or brachiocephalic ( = 44) arteriovenous fistulas. Indications for apheresis were elevated lipoprotein(a) levels ( = 26) and dyslipoproteinemia ( = 3). Mean age was comparable between groups (61.4 vs 61.2 years), as was the proportion of male patients (58.6% vs 60.9%). Diabetes mellitus was present in 58.6% of apheresis patients and 49.4% of haemodialysis patients. Two-year primary patency rates were comparable between groups (49.2% vs 50.8%), while secondary patency was lower in the apheresis group (59.9% vs 71.1%). In the apheresis cohort, diabetes was associated with reduced primary (HR, 4.034; 95 % CI, 1.10-14.80; = 0.035) and secondary patency (HR, 9.807; 95 % CI, 1.24-77.59; = 0.030). Apheresis before fistula creation demonstrated improved secondary patency (HR, 0.198; 95% CI, 0.04-0.94; = 0.042). In haemodialysis patients, hyperlipoproteinemia was associated with reduced secondary patency (HR, 2.28; 95% CI, 1.01-5.14; = 0.046). CONCLUSIONS: Arteriovenous fistula patency in patients undergoing apheresis was comparable to haemodialysis patients despite elevated lipoprotein levels. Diabetes was associated with reduced fistula patency in lipoprotein apheresis. The findings support arteriovenous fistulas as long-term access option and highlight the importance of individualised access planning.

Treatment algorithms and patient characteristics differ between haemodialysis and apheresis therapy, and fistula outcomes in patients receiving lipoprotein apheresis have not yet been systematically evaluated. METHODS: This single-centre, retrospective cohort study compared arteriovenous fistula outcomes in 29 patients receiving lipoprotein apheresis with those of 87 frequency-matched patients on haemodialysis.

title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy Is Associated With Lower Risk of Lower Extremity Amputation in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes and Foot Ulcer Without Coded Peripheral Arterial Disease: A Hypothesis-Generating Real-World Cohort Study.
abstract: AIMS: To compare lower extremity amputation (LEA) risk in adults with Type 2 diabetes and diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) treated with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) versus other glucose-lowering therapy, and to test whether coded peripheral arterial disease (PAD) modifies this association and replicates across comparator classes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This new-user, active-comparator retrospective cohort study used the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network (queried 11 July 2026). Adults with Type 2 diabetes and DFU were propensity-score matched 1:1 on 22 covariates, giving 21 325 pairs for the primary comparison. Effect modification by coded PAD (ICD-10 I70.2) was examined in independently matched subgroups. Six sensitivity analyses were pre-specified: 30- and 180-day landmarks, all-cause mortality, background-therapy balancing, limb-severity adjustment and a broadened PAD definition. RESULTS: GLP-1 RA use was associated with lower 5-year LEA risk than all non-GLP-1 RA therapy (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.60, 95% CI: 0.54-0.67). The association was confined to the no-PAD stratum (HR: 0.21, 0.13-0.33) and absent where PAD was coded (HR: 0.97, 0.78-1.20); ratio of hazard ratios 0.21 (0.13-0.36; p < 0.001). All-cause mortality was also lower (HR: 0.48, 0.45-0.50). The insulin no-PAD estimate persisted under background-therapy balancing (0.14), limb-severity adjustment (0.16) and 30- and 180-day landmarks (0.28, 0.33). Broadening the PAD definition attenuated the no-PAD association without abolishing it (HR: 0.34, 0.17-0.65). CONCLUSIONS: In Type 2 diabetes with DFU, GLP-1 RA use was associated with lower LEA risk, surviving six pre-specified sensitivity analyses. These observational findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective confirmation.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This new-user, active-comparator retrospective cohort study used the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network (queried 11 July 2026). title: "Not so minor" - Digital Amputation as a precursor to Major Amputation and Mortality in an Irish tertiary vascular centre.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Minor (toe) amputations are a common consequence of peripheral arterial disease (PAD) and/or diabetes. They can herald further forefoot and major amputations and are a poor prognostic indicator for five-year survival. This study aimed to identify prognostic indicators for progression from minor amputation to major amputation and all-cause mortality. METHODS: Index digital amputations performed by vascular surgeons in a tertiary referral hospital between 2017-2022 were identified from Hospital In-Patient Enquiry (HIPE) data. Electronic records for each limb were followed up to October 2025 for further ipsilateral minor and major amputations and mortality. RESULTS: 224 limbs in 209 patients underwent at least one minor amputation. The cohort was predominantly male (86%) with a mean age of 66.3 years (± 12.7). 70% had PAD and 80% had diabetes. In total, 34% (n=73/215) required further ipsilateral amputation, 78.3% of which occurred within 12 months of index surgery. Minor and major re-amputation rates were 25.6% and 11%, respectively. Predictors of further amputation at any level included ischaemic heart disease (IHD) (OR 2.796, 95% CI 1.54-5.06), diabetes (OR 2.31, 95% CI 1.04-5.136) and dialysis (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.021-4.915). Index hallux amputation, IHD, and revascularisation at index admission were risk factors for further major ipsilateral amputation. All-cause mortality was 11.4%, 24.8% and 48% at one, three and five years, respectively. CONCLUSION: Consistent with international data, minor amputations are poor prognostic factor for limb loss and death. In this cohort, patients with IHD and dialysis were most at risk for further amputation.

title: Comparative Outcomes of Endovascular and Open Surgical Repair for Extracranial Carotid Artery Aneurysms: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Extracranial carotid artery aneurysms (ECAAs) are rare lesions managed by open surgical repair (OpR) or endovascular repair (ER). We compared the perioperative and long-term outcomes of both strategies. METHODS: A PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis, registered in PROSPERO, was performed. Comparative studies were pooled using random-effects models, and separate single-arm meta-analyses were conducted for OpR and ER. RESULTS: Twenty-six retrospective studies involving 707 patients and 725 procedures were included (574 OpR and 151 ER). Six comparative studies (228 procedures) showed no significant differences between ER and OpR in 30-day mortality (OR, 2.58; 95% CI, 0.53-12.52), 30-day stroke (OR, 1.08; 95% CI, 0.30-3.91), late stroke, reintervention, or primary patency. In the single-arm analyses, pooled 30-day mortality and stroke rates after OpR were 1.18% and 4.29%, respectively. No 30-day deaths and one stroke were reported after ER, yielding a pooled stroke rate of 1.25% (95% CI, 0.18-8.34). Primary patency was high after both OpR (98.44%) and ER (94.50%). CONCLUSIONS: Observational evidence suggests similar perioperative outcomes and similar observed late event rates for ER and OpR in ECAAs, although heterogeneous follow-up and the absence of time-to-event analyses limit formal comparison of long-term durability. Both approaches were associated with low mortality, stroke, reintervention rates, and excellent primary patency. Open repair remains supported by a larger body of evidence and longer follow-up, whereas evidence for ER remains comparatively limited. Because treatment allocation in the available studies was influenced by patient characteristics, anatomical complexity, and surgical risk, the observed similarity in outcomes should not be interpreted as evidence of therapeutic equivalence. Given the observational design and the predominantly moderate to serious risk of bias of the included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution.

title: Postoperative complications following carotid endarterectomy are differentially impacted by sex and plaque instability.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to provide novel evidence on the role of sex and plaque instability in post-carotid endarterectomy outcomes. Current clinical guidelines regarding recommendation for carotid endarterectomy rely solely on grade of stenosis and cerebrovascular symptomatology, despite emerging evidence emphasizing the role of sex and plaque instability in determining postoperative outcomes. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of an ongoing cohort study of males and females undergoing carotid endarterectomy for clinical indications. We performed multivariable binary logistic regression to examine the relationship of biological sex and plaque instability with postoperative outcomes. RESULTS: Data of 394 participants (31% female) were analyzed. Plaque instability was independently associated with decreased odds of hemorrhagic complications at 1 month and 1 year post-surgery, as well as with decreased respiratory complications at 1 year post-surgery. Plaque features accounting for these associations were lipid core, cap infiltration, and plaque inflammation. Female sex was independently associated with increased odds of restenosis at 1 month and 1 year post-surgery. Additionally, females with unstable plaques had more cerebrovascular complications at 1 month than males with unstable plaques, and females with stable plaques had double the odds of any complication at 1 month compared with males with unstable plaques. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings show that sex and plaque instability differentially impact post-endarterectomy outcomes, with males with unstable plaques experiencing the least postoperative complications. Sex and plaque instability may therefore be important factors that play a role in postoperative complications, highlighting their importance in the context of surgical decision-making.

title: Endovascular Iliac Stenting versus Open Aortobifemoral Bypass for Aortoiliac Occlusive Disease: A Retrospective Multicentre Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aortoiliac occlusive disease (AIOD) causing chronic or critical limb-threatening ischaemia can be treated by open aortobifemoral bypass (ABF) or endovascular reconstruction. Comparative-effectiveness data adjusted for treatment-selection bias remain limited. This multicentre study compared mid-term outcomes of endovascular versus open reconstruction for AIOD. METHODS: Retrospective, non-randomised cohort study of 171 patients with AIOD (Rutherford 3-6) treated at three centres (UK, Ireland, Egypt) between January 2023 and February 2026. Outcomes were primary patency, freedom from reintervention (FFR), amputation-free survival (AFS), overall survival, and perioperative complications. Cox regression and inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting (IPTW) were used to adjust for confounding. RESULTS: 125 patients (73.1%) underwent endovascular treatment and 46 (26.9%) open bypass. Endovascular patients were older (66.8 vs 60.8 years, p<0.001) and had a lower burden of TASC C-D disease (53.6% vs 93.5%, p<0.001). Primary patency at 24 months was 62.7% vs 91.8% (log-rank p<0.001; IPTW-adjusted HR 5.67, 95% CI 1.75-18.37). Freedom from reintervention at 24 months was 63.1% vs 93.3% (p<0.001). Amputation-free survival (85.0% vs 87.4%, p=0.992) and overall survival (93.3% vs 90.0%, p=0.335) were comparable between groups. Wound infection was less frequent after endovascular treatment (0.8% vs 10.9%, p=0.006). Major amputation was independently predicted by CLTI presentation (OR 4.0) and age, not treatment group. Progressive infrainguinal disease, rather than failure of proximal revascularisation, accounted for most amputations in both groups. CONCLUSION: Open bypass confers a substantial mid-term patency and reintervention-free survival advantage over endovascular reconstruction for AIOD, most pronounced in TASC D and CLTI subgroups, without a corresponding difference in limb salvage or survival. These findings support risk-stratified rather than uniformly endovascular-first treatment selection, pending confirmation from the ongoing EVOCC randomised trial.

title: Distinct Temporal Patterns of Limb Loss and Mortality After Transcatheter Arterialization of the Deep Veins for No-Option CLTI.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: No-option chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) represents the most advanced stage of peripheral arterial disease, characterized by exhausted revascularization options and substantial systemic comorbidity. Contemporary registry data have reported amputation-free survival (AFS) as low as approximately 37% at 1 year with standard care alone. Deep venous arterialization (DVA) has emerged as a limb-salvage strategy for these patients by arterializing the venous circulation to restore perfusion to the distal extremity. Although early trial data have been encouraging, the durability of Transcatheter Arterialization of the Deep Veins (TADV) in routine clinical practice beyond the trial setting remains incompletely defined. We evaluated 2-year technical and clinical outcomes following TADV in a single-center cohort. METHODS: We performed a retrospective, single-center cohort study of 29 consecutive patients with no-option CLTI who underwent TADV, with follow-up extending up to 2 years. Outcomes assessed included technical success, 30-day circuit patency, major amputation, limb salvage, all-cause mortality, and amputation-free survival (AFS). Kaplan-Meier methods were used to estimate time-to-event outcomes, and univariable Cox regression was used to identify baseline factors associated with AFS and mortality. RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in all 29 patients (100%). During the follow-up, limb salvage was maintained in 22 of 29 patients (75.9%) (Table 2). The Kaplan-Meier limb-salvage curve plateaued after approximately 7 months, with no major amputations observed among patients who remained amputation-free beyond this point (Figure 1). All-cause mortality was 41.4% (12 of 29 patients) and increased throughout follow-up (Table 2). Older age was significantly associated with mortality (median, 77 vs 71 years; P = .047), and congestive heart failure showed a nonsignificant trend toward increased mortality risk (83.3% vs 47.1%; P = .064) (Table 3). CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort of patients with no-option CLTI, TADV achieved durable limb preservation in approximately three-quarters of patients through 2 years of follow-up, with amputation occurring almost exclusively within the first several months after the procedure. All-cause mortality remained substantial throughout follow-up, consistent with the comorbidity burden of this population. These findings support TADV as a limb-salvage option for patients with no-option CLTI who would otherwise face major amputation, although larger multicenter studies are needed to confirm long-term durability.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Predicting Amputation and Related Outcomes in Peripheral Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) affects over 236 million individuals globally and carries substantial risks of amputation, major adverse limb events (MALE), and mortality. Existing clinical scoring systems focus on short-term surgical outcomes and lack generalizability. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising tool for PAD outcome prediction. OBJECTIVE: To conduct the first quantitative meta-analysis evaluating the discriminative performance, methodological rigor, and certainty of evidence of ML-based prognostic models for adverse limb outcomes in PAD. METHODS: Following PRISMA/PRISMA-S guidelines, PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception through March 15, 2026. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and PROBAST risk-of-bias assessment. Random-effects meta-analysis (DerSimonian-Laird with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman correction) and hierarchical summary ROC (HSROC) analysis were performed; certainty was rated with GRADE. RESULTS: 2 Ten studies were included. The pooled AUC for amputation-related outcomes was 0.88 (95% CI, 0.83-0.94; prediction interval, 0.79-0.98) with substantial heterogeneity (I= 95.4%). HSROC yielded pooled sensitivity 0.855 and specificity 0.836. Registry-based studies showed higher pooled AUC than non-registry studies (0.92 vs 0.80; p = 0.004). All models had high or unclear risk of bias in the analysis domain; none underwent independent external validation. GRADE certainty was very low. CONCLUSIONS: ML models demonstrate high discriminative performance for predicting amputation-related outcomes in PAD, but very low certainty of evidence, absence of external validation, and high risk of bias currently limit clinical implementation. Prospective multicenter validation and adherence to AI reporting guidelines are essential before clinical translation.

title: Non-General Anesthesia for Endovascular Aneurysm Repair: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Clinical Outcomes and Robustness of Evidence.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The optimal anesthetic strategy for endovascular aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR) remains debated. While recent meta-analyses suggested potential benefits for non-general anesthesia (Non-GA), available evidence is observational, and the robustness of pooled estimates remains uncertain. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative observational studies (2015-2025) was conducted across PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus. Primary outcomes were 30-day and in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included length of stay (LOS) and postoperative complications. Random-effects models utilized the Paule-Mandel estimator with Hartung-Knapp adjustment, prediction intervals, and prespecified influence diagnostics. RESULTS: 2 2 Twenty-two studies comprising >150,000 EVAR procedures were analyzed. Non-GA was not associated with reduced 30-day mortality compared with general anesthesia (RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.54-1.52; I≈86%; wide prediction interval). Influence diagnostics identified one influential study; its exclusion yielded a lower mortality for Non-GA (RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.59-0.87; I≈1%). Non-GA was associated with a modest reduction in hospital LOS (mean difference -0.53 days, 95% CI -1.02 to -0.03), but no consistent differences were observed in ICU stay or major complications. The overall certainty of evidence was judged very low (GRADE). CONCLUSIONS: Non-GA for EVAR does not increase 30-day mortality risk compared to general anesthesia. However, survival estimates are sensitive to study-level characteristics and procedural complexity. Current observational evidence supports individualized anesthetic selection rather than proving superiority or equivalence of either technique.

title: Association between increased superficial calcification clusters in carotid atherosclerosis and cardiovascular events after carotid artery stenting: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The role of calcification in carotid atherosclerosis before and after carotid artery stenting (CAS) remains controversial. This study assessed the association between the extent of calcification in target carotid plaques and outcomes after CAS. METHODS: A total of 292 subjects with carotid stenosis who underwent CAS were retrospectively enrolled. Follow-up for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) was conducted via outpatient visits and telephone. Ultimately, 211 subjects completed 2-year follow-up. Superficial calcification clusters were counted on CTA. Subjects with ≥4 superficial calcification clusters (n=24) were matched in a 1:4 ratio to those with <4 superficial calcification clusters (n=96). Sensitivity analysis was performed based on the matched cohort. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 1.92 years, 14 MACEs occurring more than 30 days after discharge were recorded. In univariate Cox analysis, symptom status (P= 0.0116), alcohol abuse (P= 0.0091), total number of calcification clusters (P= 0.0428), and number of superficial calcification clusters (P= 0.0022) were significantly associated with MACEs. In bivariate analyses, the number of superficial calcification clusters maintained a reasonably good association with MACEs. In sensitivity analysis, superficial calcification clusters remained significantly associated with MACE when loss to follow-up was classified as MACE (P= 0.0256, HR= 1.2548, 95% CI 1.0281-1.5315) or as no MACE (P= 0.0265, HR= 1.4948, 95% CI 1.0479-2.1323). CONCLUSION: The number of superficial calcification clusters may independently serve as a prognostic risk factor in patients with carotid atherosclerosis undergoing CAS.

title: Outcomes of Open vs Endovascular Repair of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Involving the Iliac Bifurcation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aneurysmal involvement of the iliac bifurcation increases the complexity of both open and endovascular repair of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA), potentially raising the risk of postoperative complications. Randomized trials comparing endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) and open aortic repair (OAR) for AAA showed that EVAR is associated with a lower postoperative mortality rate. However, it remains unclear whether these results apply to AAA involving the iliac bifurcation (AAAIB). Several small single-institutional studies have shown conflicting results. This study aims to compare the outcomes of EVAR and OAR for AAAIB in a real-world, multi-institutional setting. METHODS: The Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database was queried for patients who underwent repair for AAAIB. The cohort was divided into two groups based on the intervention: EVAR vs OAR. Baseline demographic, clinical, and perioperative characteristics, as well as outcomes such as overall 30-day mortality, in-hospital mortality, Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE: death, myocardial infarction, stroke), intestinal ischemia, overall reinterventions, and 1-year survival, were compared between the groups. Univariable analysis, multivariable inverse probability-weighted regression (IPWR), survival analysis with the Kaplan-Meier method, log-rank test, and Cox proportional hazards regression were performed. RESULTS: Of all reviewed patients, 7,535 were included in the final analysis, of whom 5,742 (76.2%) underwent EVAR, whereas 1,793 (23.8%) underwent OAR. In IPWR models, patients who underwent EVAR had significantly lower odds of overall in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.25, 95%CI: 0.18-0.34, p<0.001), 30-day mortality (OR: 0.31, 95%CI: 0.23-0.42, p<0.001), MACE (OR: 0.24, 95%CI: 0.19-0.31, p<0.001), and other postoperative adverse events compared to OAR. The Cox proportional hazards model demonstrated a significantly higher 1-year survival rate for EVAR compared to OAR (HR: 0.61, 95% CI: 0.50-0.76, p<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world, multi-institutional study, EVAR for AAAIB was associated with lower odds of overall in-hospital mortality, 30-day mortality, MACE, as well as a higher 1-year survival rate, compared to the OAR. EVAR should be considered the primary method for repairing aortoiliac aneurysm involving the iliac bifurcation in anatomically suitable patients. Longer follow-up studies are needed to confirm these findings and compare the long-term reintervention and aorta-related mortality rates between the two treatment modalities.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of the BlueDop Vascular Expert for detecting peripheral arterial disease in people with suspected intermittent claudication referred to secondary care: A cross-sectional study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Manual ankle-brachial pressure index (ABI) assessment requires significant time and expertise, precluding its use in primary care. Automated vascular assessment tools may offer a simple and efficient alternative for detecting peripheral arterial disease (PAD). However, further evidence is needed before they can be recommended. This study considers the diagnostic accuracy of the BlueDop Vascular Expert (BVE) in people with suspected intermittent claudication. METHODS: We performed a cross-sectional cohort study including people referred to our nurse-led intermittent claudication clinic. BVE measurements were compared to the manual resting ABI/TBI method, using traditional cut-off values of <0.9 and <0.7, respectively. RESULTS: 217 participants and 430 limbs were included, with an overall PAD prevalence of 46%. Sensitivity, specificity, positive (PPV) and negative predictor values (NPV) for the BVE were 88.5%, 80.7%, 81.3% and 88.1% respectively, when compared to the manual ABI. When compared to the manual TBI, the sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV for the BVE were 45.5%, 88%, 62.5% and 78.6% respectively, though this analysis included only 38 limbs. No BVE diagnoses were based on ABI alone, 71% were based on waveform alone and 29% were based on a combination of ABI and waveform. The BVE assessment was significantly quicker to perform than the manual method (p<0.01). CONCLUSION: The BVE demonstrated favourable sensitivity and specificity for detecting or excluding PAD compared to the manual ABI. Further work is needed comparing this device to others, across a range of clinical populations and settings before it can be considered in routine clinical practice.

title: Clinical Outcomes and Exploratory Haemodynamic Numerical Simulation of Patients with Multichannelled Aortic Dissection: A Multicentre, Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Multichannelled aortic dissection (MCAD) is a rare type of aortic dissection with limited data on its clinical features and outcomes. This multicentre, retrospective cohort study compared clinical outcomes between MCAD and double channelled aortic dissection (DCAD) and explored haemodynamic differences. METHODS: Patients with aortic dissection were enrolled from three tertiary hospitals. Patients with one true lumen and one false lumen were classified as having DCAD, whereas those with one true lumen and multiple false lumina were classified as having MCAD. Propensity score matching balanced baseline characteristics. Primary outcomes were 30 day and five year all cause mortality after diagnosis. Secondary outcomes included preprocedural mortality, aortic dissection related mortality, post-operative complications, and re-intervention. Overall survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Haemodynamic differences were evaluated by exploratory computational fluid dynamics (CFD) analysis. RESULTS: After matching, 50 patients were included in each group (n = 100). The difference in 30 day mortality was significant (p = .046) and largely reflected preprocedural deaths, which occurred in six patients with MCAD (12%) and none with DCAD (p = .027). Overall survival differed between groups (log rank p = .037; hazard ratio 2.72, 95% confidence interval 1.03 - 7.18; p = .044). Kaplan-Meier estimated mortality at 30 days, one year, and five years was 16%, 23%, and 29% in MCAD compared with 4%, 8%, and 12% in DCAD, respectively. Among treated patients, re-intervention was more frequent in MCAD than in DCAD (21% vs. 6%; p = .036), whereas post-operative complication rates did not differ. Exploratory CFD analysis suggested greater false lumen haemodynamic burden in MCAD. CONCLUSION: MCAD was associated with greater preprocedural mortality and more frequent re-intervention than DCAD. These findings may identify MCAD as a higher risk phenotype warranting closer surveillance and timely evaluation. Haemodynamic observations remain exploratory and require validation in larger prospective cohorts.

title: Endoscopic versus open great saphenous vein harvesting for lower extremity arterial bypass: A systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare postoperative outcomes of patients undergoing lower extremity arterial bypass (LEAB) for peripheral artery disease (PAD) with endoscopic great saphenous vein harvest (EVH) versus open vein harvest (OVH), and to investigate the impact of publication year on bypass patency. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched from inception through January 2025 for comparative studies of EVH versus OVH in LEAB. Individual patient data were reconstructed from Kaplan-Meier curves and analysed using Cox proportional hazards models. Binary and continuous outcomes were pooled using random-effects models. Meta-regression and subgroup analyses by publication year (≤2015 vs >2015) were performed to explore temporal trends in patency. RESULTS: 2 Thirteen retrospective cohort studies comprising 12 401 patients were included. EVH was associated with higher risk of primary patency loss compared with OVH (HR 1.32; 95% CI 1.04-1.68; p=.030) and a borderline longer operative time (MD 58.98 minutes; 95% CI 0.63-117.32; p=.050; I=96%), but significantly lower wound complications (RR 0.68; 95% CI 0.57-0.80; p<.001). No differences were observed in primary-assisted patency, secondary patency, length of stay, major amputation, limb salvage, or mortality. Subgroup analysis showed that the primary patency disadvantage was driven by studies published up to 2015 (HR 1.49; p=.010), with no significant difference in studies published after 2015 (HR 0.97; p=.900), although the interaction test was not significant (p=.100). Meta-regression did not demonstrate an association between publication year and primary patency effect size (p=.890). CONCLUSION: EVH significantly reduces wound complications but is associated with lower primary patency and potentially longer operative times compared with OVH, disadvantages that do not translate into differences in secondary patency, limb salvage, major amputation, or mortality. Further prospective studies are needed to define the role of EVH to better inform LEAB operative planning.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Transperitoneal vs Retroperitoneal Approaches of Open Aortic Repair for Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Stratified by the Iliac Bifurcation Involvement.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aortic aneurysm involving the iliac bifurcation (AAAIB) is associated with higher rates of systemic comorbidities and increased complexity of open aortic repair (OAR), resulting in worse outcomes compared to OAR for isolated abdominal aortic aneurysm (IAAA). The Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) practice guidelines recommend the retroperitoneal approach (RPA) for OAR in certain patients with abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). However, there is limited evidence to determine whether the relative advantages and disadvantages of RPA and the transperitoneal approach (TPA) change depending on whether the aneurysm distally involves the iliac bifurcation. This study aims to compare the outcomes of TPA and RPA for AAA, stratified by the iliac bifurcation involvement, in a multi-institutional, real-world setting. METHODS: The SVS Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database was queried for patients who underwent OAR for AAA from January 2003 to September 2024. Patients were stratified as AAAIB or IAAA based on whether the aneurysm involved the iliac bifurcation and required a distal anastomosis beyond the common iliac artery (CIA) bifurcation, or not. Baseline characteristics, as well as outcomes such as overall 30-day mortality, Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE: death, myocardial infarction, stroke), and 1-year survival, were compared between the TPA and RPA groups in patients with IAAA and AAAIB. Univariable and multivariable analyses, as well as a confirmatory analysis with inverse probability-weighted regression (IPWR), were performed. RESULTS: Of all reviewed patients, 17,009 were included in the final analysis, of whom 15,218 (89.5%) had IAAA, and 1,791 (10.5%) had AAAIB. Among patients with IAAA, compared to RPA, TPA was associated with higher odds of overall 30-day mortality (OR: 1.26, 95%CI: 1.05-1.49, p=0.011), MACE (OR: 1.26, 95%CI: 1.11-1.44, p=0.001), and a lower 1-year survival rate (HR: 1.23, 95%CI: 1.09-1.39, p=0.001). Among patients with AAAIB, TPA was associated with lower odds of lower extremity (LE) ischemia (OR: 0.47, 95%CI: 0.25-0.91, p=0.024) without significant differences in 30-day mortality (OR: 0.80, 95%CI: 0.42-1.51, p=0.485), MACE (OR: 0.86, 95%CI: 0.52-1.42, p=0.563), and 1-year survival (HR: 0.93, 95%CI: 0.59-1.47, p=0.768). CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world study, involvement of the iliac bifurcation in AAA was an effect modifier for the outcomes of different OAR approaches. For patients with IAAA, compared with RPA, TPA was associated with worse 30-day mortality, MACE, and 1-year survival. Whereas for patients with AAAIB, TPA was associated with lower odds of LE ischemia, without significant differences in 30-day mortality, MACE, or 1-year survival. This study suggests that RPA may be the procedure of choice for IAAA if it is otherwise feasible. However, TPA may be the procedure of choice for patients with AAAIB who are otherwise anatomically suitable. Larger prospective studies are warranted to validate these findings.

title: Prevalence of Guideline-Recommended Genetic Testing in Patients at Risk for Heritable Thoracic Aortic Disease.
abstract: Heritable thoracic aortic diseases (HTAD) include genetic conditions that increase risk of thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection. The 2022 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) guidelines recommend genetic testing for at-risk individuals, but real-world uptake remains unclear. We evaluated adherence to testing recommendations and demographic differences across major HTAD risk cohorts. We conducted a retrospective study using the TriNetX Research Network (2005-2025). Three guideline-based cohorts were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes: (1) thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection before age 60, (2) family history of thoracic aortic disease, and (3) non-thoracic arterial aneurysms. Genetic testing was defined by ICD-10-CM codes for genetic screening or susceptibility. Testing prevalence was stratified by age, sex, race, and ethnicity, and annual testing incidence (2005-2024) was evaluated. Among 57,935 patients with thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection before age 60, 1,205 (2.09%) underwent genetic testing. Among 2,811,862 patients with a family history of thoracic aortic disease, 66,699 (2.38%) received testing. Among 347,000 patients with non-thoracic arterial aneurysms, 4,913 (1.42%) underwent testing. Testing was consistently higher in females than males and varied across age groups. Annual testing incidence increased over time but remained <0.6% by 2024. In conclusion, genetic testing for HTAD remains markedly underutilized, with < 2.5% of at-risk patients tested despite guideline recommendations, highlighting persistent implementation gaps and the need to improve equitable access to genetic evaluation.

title: Outcomes of hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation (HEPATIC): an international, multicentre, retrospective registry study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation is a severe complication that can lead to acute graft failure, often requiring urgent re-transplantation. We aimed to assess the 1-year incidence of graft loss and mortality and to evaluate outcomes according to the timing of hepatic artery thrombosis and the treatment approaches in patients with hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation. METHODS: In this international, multicentre, retrospective study, the HEPATIC registry, which had 33 centres across 21 countries as of December, 2025, was used to identify patients who developed hepatic artery thrombosis at age younger than 18 years after paediatric liver transplantation between Jan 1, 2002, and Dec 31, 2021, and who either received a diagnosis of or received an intervention for hepatic artery thrombosis before Jan 1, 2023. Donor-related, recipient-related, and transplantation-related characteristics collected from local medical records were entered retrospectively into electronic case reports by participating centres, with centralised data quality control. Primary outcomes were 1-year graft loss and mortality after hepatic artery thrombosis diagnosis. The outcomes were examined based on when hepatic artery thrombosis occurred after paediatric liver transplantation (early [≤7 days] vs late [>7 days]), primary management strategy (conservative management, surgical revascularisation, endovascular therapy, or immediate listing for re-transplantation), and transplantation era (in 5-year intervals). The registry was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05818644. FINDINGS: Hepatic artery thrombosis occurred in 415 patients, of whom 216 (52%) were female and 199 (48%) were male, and median age was 1·7 years (IQR 0·8-6·5). Median follow-up was 50·9 months (IQR 17·0-112·6). Graft loss occurred in 180 patients by 1 month (cumulative incidence 43% [95% CI 38-48]) and 222 by 1 year (54% [49-58]); 51 patients died by 1 month (12% [9-15]) and 77 by 1 year (19% [15-22]). Surgical revascularisation was the first-line treatment approach in 195 (47%) patients. Other strategies included listing for re-transplantation in 99 (24%), conservative management in 79 (19%), and endovascular therapy in 42 (10%). Treatment approaches changed over time, with increased use of conservative management and endovascular therapy and reduced listing for re-transplantation (p<0·0001), with no accompanying change in 1-year mortality across eras (p=0·14). Early (≤7 days) hepatic artery thrombosis occurred in 282 (68%) patients and was associated with higher 1-year graft loss than late (>7 days) hepatic artery thrombosis (cumulative incidence 57% [95% CI 51-63] vs 47% [37-55], log-rank p=0·010). Surgical revascularisation was used in 167 (59%) patients and listing for re-transplantation in 66 (23%) patients with early hepatic artery thrombosis, whereas conservative management was used in 51 (38%) patients and endovascular therapy in 21 (16%) patients with late hepatic artery thrombosis; however, 1-year mortality did not differ between treatment strategies among patients with early versus late hepatic artery thrombosis. INTERPRETATION: Hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation is associated with notably high 1-year graft loss and mortality, particularly if hepatic artery thrombosis occurs within 7 days after the procedure. The management strategies for hepatic artery thrombosis differ according to the post-transplantation timing of hepatic artery thrombosis occurrence. Despite changes in management over the past 20 years, outcomes have remained poor, underscoring the need to improve therapeutic strategies for this complication. FUNDING: None.

title: Retrograde access revascularization in chronic limb threatening ischaemia.
abstract: PURPOSE: Chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI) is associated with high rates of major amputation, mortality and comorbidity that can make conventional femoral access challenging or contraindicated; in particular in patients with recent groin surgery, infection, previous aorto-bifemoral stent reconstruction, hostile groins, or unfavourable body habitus. Tibio-pedal arterial minimally invasive retrograde revascularisation (TAMI) provides an alternative access strategy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-centre cohort study included 84 TAMI procedures in 81 limbs from 77 patients with CLTI (median age 72 years; 64% male; Rutherford IV 22%; Rutherford V-VI 78%). TAMI was performed because of recent groin surgery/infection in 35% of procedures and patient-related factors in 65%. The primary clinical endpoint was freedom from major adverse limb events (MALE), defined as major amputation or clinically driven target-vessel reintervention (CDTVR). Secondary endpoints included technical success, defined as restoration of continuous inline flow through at least one infrapopliteal artery to the foot with < 50% residual stenosis on completion angiography, and access vessel safety. RESULTS: Retrograde access was obtained predominantly via the dorsalis pedis (71%) and distal posterior tibial arteries (16%). Technical success was achieved in 66/84 procedures (78%); in 10/84 (12%), TAMI access and lesion crossing were successful but the predefined angiographic endpoint was not met, while eight procedures (10%) were abandoned. Asymptomatic access vessel spasm was documented in 35/84 procedures (42%) that had resolved by 24 h. Among 68 patients (71 limbs) with longitudinal follow-up, median follow-up was 150 days (IQR 76-322). CDTVR occurred in 22/71 limbs (30%) and major amputation in 14/71 (20%); 25/68 patients (37%) died. Kaplan-Meier estimated freedom from MALE was 57.9% (95% CI 43.9-69.6%) at 6 months and 51.2% (95% CI 36.0-64.5%) at 12 months. In multivariable Cox regression analysis, none of the evaluated covariates was significantly associated with MALE. CONCLUSION: In this selected, anatomically complex CLTI cohort, TAMI was a feasible alternative access strategy when conventional femoral access was challenging or not feasible, with a low observed rate of clinically significant pedal access complications.

title: Protocol-based medical management for inflammatory abdominal aortic aneurysms: a five-year single-center experience.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Inflammatory abdominal aortic aneurysm (IAAA), a distinct clinical entity characterized by dense periaortic fibrosis and elevated inflammatory markers, lacks a consensus-driven optimal management strategy. While medical therapy is often utilized, comparative data against surgical or endovascular interventions remain limited. We report our experience with a standardized medical protocol for the management of IAAAs. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 27 consecutive patients diagnosed with IAAA between 2012 and 2019. Predefined diagnostic criteria for IAAA included an ESR>100 mm/h, aortic wall thickness >10 mm, and inflammatory symptoms. Risk of rupture was assessed using a PET-CT scan for patients with a maximal aortic diameter exceeding 5.5 cm. A standardized medical protocol was used for low rupture risk patients including IV methylprednisolone followed by oral prednisone taper. Methotrexate was introduced for steroid-refractory cases. Endovascular or open aortic repair was used for patients with high risk of rupture. RESULTS: Patients had a mean age of 62.3 years, and 70.4% were male. The mean baseline aortic diameter was 48±5 mm (95% CI 46.0-50.0). Twenty-three patients (85.2%) were treated initially with corticosteroids. At the 3-month mark, 69.6% of medically treated patients achieved an acceptable response with steroids alone. Five steroid-refractory patients received methotrexate and demonstrated clinical improvement. ESR normalized in 95.7% of medically treated patients. During five-year follow-up, no medically managed patient required emergency surgical intervention. Eleven patients required temporary steroid reintroduction at 3 years, with sustained stability at 5 years. Three patients underwent EVAR with favorable outcomes. One patient underwent open repair, which was associated with significant perioperative morbidity and late mortality. CONCLUSIONS: In selected patients with low risk of aortic rupture, protocol-based medical therapy for IAAA is safe and effective with minimal risk upon mid-term follow-up. PET-CT scan assessment for risk of immediate rupture is appropriate for patients with aortic diameter between 5.5 to 6.5 cm. Methotrexate introduction may be effective for steroid-refractory cases. Endovascular repair remains a suitable option when intervention is required. Larger prospective studies are needed to establish definitive management guidelines for IAAAs.

title: Bailout stenting strategy in complex femoropopliteal lesions: mid-term outcomes with drug-eluting versus bare-metal stents.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The aim of this study was to compare mid-term outcomes of drug-eluting stents (DES) versus bare-metal stents (BMS) when used as a bailout strategy for complex femoropopliteal lesions in real-world practice. METHODS: Single-center, retrospective cohort (January 2018 - February 2025) including patients requiring bailout stenting after suboptimal angioplasty. Primary endpoints included primary patency, freedom from clinically driven target lesion revascularization (cdTLR). Secondary endpoints were considered the limb loss, freedom from major adverse limb events (MALE) and all-cause mortality rate. Time-to-event outcomes were analyzed by Kaplan-Meier and log-rank testing up to 36 months; hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated. A multivariable Cox model explored predictors of statistically significant outcomes. RESULTS: 2 2 2 2 2 A total of 141 patients were included (BMS 65; DES 76). Compared with DES, the BMS group had higher rates of diabetes (58.5% vs. 40.8, P=0.036), CKD (70.8% vs. 40.8, P<0.001), dialysis (12.3% vs. 1.3, P=0.008), CLTI (89.2% vs. 75.0, P=0.030), Rutherford 5-6 (69.2% vs. 52.6, P=0.045), and ASA ≥3 (100% vs. 89.5, P=0.007). Kaplan-Meier analyses showed no significant between-group differences for primary patency (log-rank χ0.0011, P=0.973; HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.43-2.27), freedom from cdTLR (χ1.6318, P=0.2015; HR 0.52, 0.19-1.41), limb loss (χ2.37, P=0.124; HR 4.03, 0.68-23.76), or freedom from MALE (χ0.68, P=0.409; HR 1.48, 0.58-3.79). The all-cause mortality rate in the unadjusted analysis resulted higher in the BMS group (log-rank χ13.09, P<0.0003); (HR 2.75; 95% CI 1.59-4.76). In multivariable analysis, mortality was independently associated with CKD (HR 3.43, P=0.001), dialysis (HR 2.70, P=0.012), tissue loss/Rutherford 5-6 (HR 2.54, P=0.006), and history for neoplasia (HR 1.96, P=0.028); stent type was not an independent predictor (BMS vs. DES HR 0.54, P=0.063). CONCLUSIONS: In bailout setting for long, complex femoropopliteal disease, stent type did not influence the outcomes post revascularization at 36 months. The overall all-cause mortality rate was driven by baseline clinical status rather than the device.

title: Aortoduodenal syndrome: evolving management of a rare cause of duodenal obstruction in the endovascular era.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Aortoduodenal syndrome (ADS) is a very rare complication of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA), characterized by extrinsic compression of the duodenum leading to proximal bowel obstruction. This systematic review sought to aggregate all published ADS cases, with emphasis on patient demographics, diagnostic workup, treatment modalities, and outcomes. METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted across MedLine/PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science from database inception through 2 February 2026, following PRISMA guidelines. Reports containing original patient data describing duodenal obstruction attributable to abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA), irrespective of rupture status, were eligible for inclusion, provided that the obstruction was attributed to aneurysmal mass effect. Extracted variables included demographic characteristics, clinical presentation, aneurysm morphology, diagnostic imaging, therapeutic interventions, and follow-up results. This study has been registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251456530). RESULTS: n n Forty studies encompassing 44 patients were analyzed. The cohort was predominantly male (86.6%), with a mean age of 74.5 years. The most common presenting symptoms were vomiting, abdominal pain, and a palpable pulsatile abdominal mass. Computed tomography served as the primary diagnostic tool, whereas upper gastrointestinal contrast series and endoscopy were employed mainly to exclude alternative obstructive etiologies. The third duodenal portion was the most frequently compressed segment, with a median aneurysm diameter of 72.5 mm. Surgical intervention was performed in most patients, comprising open aortic repair ( = 18) or endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR, = 13). Gastrointestinal bypass procedures were reserved for selected or salvage situations. Outcome data were available for 42 patients. Mortality was reported in 6 patients (14.3%), including two patients who did not undergo operative treatment. Among the 39 patients who underwent operative treatment, postoperative complications were reported in 9 patients (23.1%). CONCLUSION: EVAR represents an increasingly reported treatment option in anatomically suitable patients, particularly those at high operative risk; however, the available evidence remains insufficient to establish EVAR as the preferred first-line treatment. Treatment should be individualized according to aneurysm anatomy, clinical condition, operative risk, and severity of duodenal obstruction.

title: Lower-extremity Deep Vein Thrombosis after Plastic Surgery: Clinical Characteristics and Outcomes in a Retrospective Case Series.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a significant complication in plastic surgery, particularly affecting the lower extremities. Understanding the associated characteristics can aid in developing effective prevention strategies. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, quality improvement-oriented case series of 5 ultrasound-confirmed symptomatic postoperative lower-extremity DVT events after plastic surgery under general anesthesia at a single institution (January 2020-May 2024). Among 39,055 general anesthesia procedures during the study period, de-identified records were reviewed for patient and procedural characteristics, prophylaxis and mobility pathways, duplex ultrasonography confirmation, management, and short-term outcomes. No non-DVT comparator cohort was extracted; analyses were descriptive and not intended for risk-factor inference. One patient with postoperative chest/back pain and transfer for suspected pulmonary embolism without in-hospital lower-extremity DVT confirmation was excluded from the final case series. RESULTS: The 5 included cases were clinically heterogeneous and involved complex perioperative settings, including post-massive weight loss body contouring, craniofacial reconstruction with implant use, neurosurgical-related reconstruction, extensive head and neck lesion surgery, and posttraumatic facial reconstruction. All DVTs were confirmed by duplex Doppler ultrasonography, with thrombi involving the posterior tibial, peroneal, or calf muscular veins. Several cases involved prolonged procedures, reoperation for postoperative hematoma, or delayed mobilization. Postoperative anticoagulation was administered in most cases, whereas postoperative mechanical prophylaxis was not consistently documented. CONCLUSIONS: In a very low-frequency setting, this series highlights potentially actionable prevention gaps-especially postoperative mechanical prophylaxis and mobility disruptions-rather than establishing causal risk factors.

title: Use of Telestroke Prior to Endovascular Stroke Treatment in Canada: Results from the OPTIMISE Registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Telestroke allows rapid assessment of acute stroke patients for intravenous thrombolysis and endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). While its safety and efficacy for thrombolysis are well established, evidence regarding EVT decision-making via telestroke is scarce. METHODS: We analysed data from Optimising Patient Treatment In Major Ischaemic Stroke with EVT (OPTIMISE), an EVT registry of Canadian comprehensive stroke centres. We compared unadjusted time metrics and procedural outcomes between patients treated with EVT evaluated via telestroke and those evaluated without telestroke. A primary analysis included all EVT cases, and a sub-analysis focused on patients transferred from another centre. Mixed-effects logistic regression, adjusted for relevant clinical and radiological confounders, was used to assess symptomatic intracerebral haemorrhage (sICH), good functional outcome and all-cause mortality. RESULTS: Between 2018 and 2021, a total of 6803 patients received EVT across 20 centres. Patients receiving telestroke consultation had longer onset-to-EVT centre door time and onset-to-groin puncture time. In unadjusted analyses, telestroke patients had higher sICH proportions (6.5% vs. 3.1%), lower proportions of good functional outcomes (35.6% vs. 40.6%) and higher all-cause mortality (39.9% vs. 27.5%) compared to those not receiving telestroke consultation. These differences did not persist in adjusted analyses. The sub-analysis with multivariate adjustment restricted to transferred patients also revealed no differences in outcomes between the two groups. CONCLUSION: Patients evaluated with telestroke prior to EVT had longer treatment times than those not evaluated with telestroke. The higher risk for unfavourable outcomes did not persist after adjustment for confounders. There remains a strong need to optimise the delivery of EVT for patients evaluated at telestroke centres.

title: Endovascular Therapy for Femoropopliteal Artery Lesions Involving the Popliteal Artery: 1-Year Outcomes from a Real-World Multicenter Registry.
abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate real-world outcomes of endovascular treatment for femoropopliteal lesions involving the popliteal artery and, in a post-hoc exploratory analysis, assess whether anatomical location (P3 vs. P1/P2 segments) was associated with clinical decision-making and prognosis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, post-hoc analysis of 946 patients from the prospective PROMISING registry. For this exploratory analysis, patients were stratified according to distal (P3) versus proximal/mid (P1/P2) popliteal artery involvement. Predictors of stent implantation and clinical decision pathways were compared across groups. RESULTS: Overall procedural success was 98.5%, and the 12-month freedom from major adverse events (MAE), defined as a composite of all-cause mortality, major amputation, or clinically driven target lesion revascularization, was 80.1%. Multivariable analysis indicated P3 involvement independently predicted reduced stent implantation (OR 0.66, 95% CI 0.46-0.95, p = 0.027). For vessel preparation, the P3 group more frequently utilized plain old balloon angioplasty (POBA, 67.8% vs. 54.8%, p < 0.001) rather than directional atherectomy or specialty balloons. Despite a lower stent implantation rate and greater use of POBA, 12-month freedom from MAE was comparable between the P3 and P1/P2 groups (78.0% vs. 81.2%, p = 0.481). CONCLUSION: In this post-hoc analysis of real-world registry data, popliteal lesion location was associated with differences in operator treatment strategies. P3 involvement was associated with less frequent stent implantation and greater use of plain balloon angioplasty, while 1-year clinical outcomes were comparable between the P3 and P1/P2 groups. These exploratory findings require external validation before they can be used to inform clinical treatment strategies. title: One-year outcomes of hepatic artery stenosis after pediatric liver transplantation: Results from the international, multicenter HEPATIC registry.
abstract: AIM: This study aimed to describe one-year graft and patient survival after hepatic artery stenosis (HAS) following pediatric liver transplantation (pLT), and to explore outcomes by timing of HAS diagnosis and treatment strategy within the HAS cohort. METHODS: Patients who developed HAS after pLT were included as per definition from the HEPATIC registry. The registry contains data from 32 centers across 21 countries over a 20-year period, during which 10,564 primary pLTs were performed. Donor-, recipient-, and transplant-related characteristics were analyzed. The primary outcome was one-year graft and patient survival. RESULTS: HAS was diagnosed in 1.2% of patients (n = 130; 51% female; median age 4.4 years [IQR 1.4-11.6]), of whom 5% (n = 7) progressed to thrombosis (HAT). One-year graft and patient survival were 93% and 96%, respectively. Management consisted mainly of antithrombotic therapy alone (41.5%) or endovascular therapy (EVT; 41.5%), with no significant difference in one-year graft or patient survival between these approaches. Early HAS (≤21 days post-pLT) was associated with significantly higher one-year graft loss than late HAS (16%vs. 1%; p < 0.001). All deaths occurred in the early HAS group. CONCLUSIONS: One-year graft and patient survival after HAS were high. Antithrombotic therapy alone and EVT were the most common management strategies. Early HAS was associated with lower one-year survival. Prospective studies with standardized diagnostic and treatment criteria are needed for validation.

title: Imaging And Outcomes In The Treatment Of Sacral Dural Arteriovenous Fistulas.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Spinal dural arteriovenous fistulas (DAVFs) in the sacral region are extremely rare and their intradural retrograde draining system has not been investigated in detail. The aim of this study was to characterize the venous drainage patterns of sacral DAVFs based on our clinical experience in treating patients with this condition. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed the clinical data of patients with sacral DAVFs treated at our institution from January 2016 to January 2024. Preoperative spinal angiography was used to evaluate the positional relationship between the shunt point of sacral DAVF and the vertebral midline. We proposed that if the location of the shunt point was located on the midline, the draining vein would be the filum terminale vein (FTV); if the shunt point was located off the midline, the draining vein would be the radiculomedullary vein (RMV). RESULTS: A total of 17 sacral DAVFs patients treated with direct surgery were included in this study. All patients presented with lower extremity weakness and numbness. Sphincter dysfunction was present in 15 patients (88.2%). The mean interval from symptom onset to diagnosis was 14.1 months (range 1-96 months). Preoperative magnetic resonance imaging(MRI) detected T2 hyperintensity at the level of the conus medullaris and intradural flow voids in all patients. Spinal angiography confirmed the diagnosis of sacral DAVF in all cases, and complete fistula occlusion was achieved with surgical ligation in all patients. Intraoperatively, 4 patients with the midline location of the shunt point were confirmed to have FTV as the draining vein, while the other 13 patients with off-midline shunt point were confirmed to have RMV as the draining vein. The intraoperative findings were completely consistent with the preoperative assessment of the draining veins based on the location of the shunt point. CONCLUSIONS: The draining veins of sacral DAVFs are not always the FTVs, in fact, most sacral DAVFs drain via the RMV. With our simple imaging-based method, the two different types of draining veins in sacral DAVFs can be preliminarily identified before surgery.

title: Preoperative white matter lesions and functional recovery after revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Restoring ambulation is an important goal of revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), but predictors of functional recovery remain limited. We investigated whether preoperative white matter lesion (WML) burden was associated with ambulatory recovery after revascularization. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 196 patients with CLTI, tissue loss, Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection (WIfI) ischemia grade 2 or 3, and brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) within 3 months before revascularization. Preoperative brain MRI was routinely obtained in patients considered for open surgical revascularization for cerebrovascular risk assessment. Periventricular and deep subcortical white matter hyperintensities were graded using the Fazekas scale; a total score of 3 or greater defined high-grade WML burden. The primary outcome was achievement of a Functional Ambulation Category score of 3 or greater within 180 days. Associations were evaluated using multivariable Cox models. RESULTS: High-grade WML burden was present in 120 patients. Six-month ambulatory recovery was lower in the high-grade group than in the low-grade group (63.1% vs 82.4%; P = .019). High-grade WML burden was independently associated with slower ambulatory recovery (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 0.65; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.43-0.96; P = .032) and delayed final discharge (adjusted HR, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.43-0.92; P = .017), but not with wound healing or wound-free functional limb achievement. CONCLUSIONS: High-grade WML burden was associated with impaired ambulatory recovery and delayed discharge after CLTI revascularization. When preoperative brain MRI is available, WML assessment may complement limb staging and help anticipate rehabilitation and discharge needs.

title: Anatomic Level as a Modifier of Racial/Ethnic Disparities in Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia: Outcomes After First-Time Endovascular Revascularization.
abstract: PURPOSE: Racial and ethnic disparities in chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) outcomes are well documented, but whether these disparities vary by anatomic level of endovascular intervention remains unclear. We evaluated racial and ethnic differences in limb outcomes following endovascular revascularization for CLTI stratified by intervention level. METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network, including adults undergoing first-time lower extremity endovascular revascularization for CLTI between 2015-2024. Patients were stratified by intervention level: iliac, femoropopliteal, tibioperoneal, or combined femoropopliteal and tibioperoneal (multilevel). Propensity score matching balanced demographics and comorbidities across racial/ethnic cohorts. The primary outcomes were rates of 1-year major amputation and amputation-free survival (AFS). Outcome comparisons were reported as risk ratios (RR). RESULTS: Among 14,786 patients, there were 3,071 iliac, 5,178 femoropopliteal, 2,363 tibioperoneal, and 3,718 multilevel interventions. After matching, Black patients demonstrated increased major amputation risk following iliac intervention (RR: 1.80, 95% CI: 1.13-2.88, p=0.012) and femoropopliteal intervention (RR: 1.83, 95% CI 1.39-2.41, p<0.001) compared with White patients. No significant differences in amputation were observed following tibioperoneal or multilevel interventions. Hispanic patients exhibited increased amputation risk only in the multilevel cohort (RR: 1.57, 95% CI: 1.02-2.40, p=0.037). Despite differences in amputation, AFS remained similar across racial and ethnic groups. CONCLUSIONS: Racial and ethnic disparities in CLTI outcomes following endovascular revascularization varied by anatomic intervention level. Disparities were most pronounced after proximal interventions and attenuated in distal disease, suggesting anatomic disease pattern may modify inequities in limb outcomes after revascularization.

title: Predicting acute kidney injury in type B aortic dissection: development and validation of a clinical nomogram.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) is a frequent and serious complication in patients with Type B Aortic Dissection (TBAD). Existing prediction models are mainly derived from type A or mixed cohorts and do not account for the distinct pathophysiology of TBAD. This study aimed to develop and validate a nomogram for individualized AKI risk prediction in TBAD patients. METHODS: Data were obtained from the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD) and the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV). The eICU-CRD cohort was used for model development and internal validation, while MIMIC-IV served for external validation. A three-step variable selection strategy combining Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO), univariate, and multivariate logistic regression analyses was applied. Model performance was evaluated using the Area Under the receiver operating characteristic Curve (AUC), calibration curves, and Decision Curve Analysis (DCA). RESULTS: Six independent predictors were identified: ICU length of stay, minimum glucose, minimum sodium, maximum bicarbonate, minimum creatinine, and minimum diastolic blood pressure. The nomogram showed excellent discrimination, with AUCs of 0.926 (95% CI: 0.893-0.956), 0.922 (95% CI: 0.869-0.967), and 0.921 (95% CI: 0.895-0.944) in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. Calibration analysis demonstrated good agreement, and DCA indicated clinical utility within a threshold probability range of 0-70%. CONCLUSIONS: This study developed a practical nomogram based on six readily available variables for dynamic in-hospital prediction of AKI in TBAD patients. The model may assist early risk stratification, although further prospective validation is warranted.

title: Incidence and Predictors of Symptomatic Thrombosis During Asparaginase-containing Therapy in Children With Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia: A Meta-analysis and Narrative Synthesis.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Symptomatic thrombosis is a clinically important complication of asparaginase-containing therapy in children with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), but reported incidence and predictors vary across studies. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to estimate its incidence and synthesize reported predictors. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through April 15, 2026. Eligible studies enrolled patients aged ≤21 years with ALL receiving asparaginase-containing therapy and reported extractable incidence or predictor data for overall symptomatic thrombosis or symptomatic venous thromboembolism. Proportions were pooled after logit transformation using a random-effects model. Predictor data were synthesized narratively when quantitative pooling was inappropriate. RESULTS: Twenty-three studies met the eligibility criteria; 15 studies involving 17,809 children and 655 events contributed to the incidence meta-analysis. The pooled incidence of symptomatic thrombosis was 5.6% (95% CI: 3.5%-9.0%), with substantial heterogeneity (I²=96.9%). Study-specific estimates ranged from ∼1% to 22.7%. Older age was the most consistently reported predictor; associations with inherited thrombophilia, non-O blood group, high-risk treatment status, and T-ALL phenotype were inconsistent across cohorts. CONCLUSIONS: Symptomatic thrombosis affects ∼6% of children with ALL receiving asparaginase-containing therapy, although incidence varies considerably across studies. Older age was the most reproducible risk factor, whereas evidence for other predictors remains heterogeneous.

title: Real-World Use and Outcomes of Post-Discharge Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis After Thoracic Cancer Operation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Post-discharge venous thromboembolism prophylaxis is conditionally recommended after thoracic cancer operation, but real-world use and associated outcomes across procedures and operative approaches remain poorly characterized. STUDY DESIGN: We conducted a retrospective Epic Cosmos cohort study of adults undergoing lung or esophageal cancer resection from 2016-2025. Post-discharge prophylaxis was defined as prophylactic-dose anticoagulation prescribed within 7 days of discharge. Thirty-day outcomes were compared using 1:3 propensity-score matching stratified by procedure and operative approach. RESULTS: Among 157,619 patients (14,277 esophagectomy; 143,342 lung resection), 11.15% and 1.48%, respectively, received post-discharge prophylaxis. After open esophagectomy, prophylaxis was associated with lower DVT (1.23% vs 2.63%; p=0.039), PE (0.46% vs 1.44%; p=0.047), and mortality (1.70% vs 5.20%; p<0.001), without significantly increased bleeding. Findings were similar after minimally invasive esophagectomy: DVT 0.32% vs 1.46% (p=0.003), PE 0.21% vs 0.89% (p=0.034), and mortality 1.28% vs 3.20% (p=0.003). After open lung resection, prophylaxis was associated with lower PE and mortality but higher bleeding and healthcare use. After minimally invasive lung resection, thromboembolic outcomes did not significantly differ, while bleeding and healthcare use were higher. Enoxaparin accounted for 79.35% of prophylaxis prescriptions; thromboembolic outcomes did not significantly differ between apixaban and enoxaparin. CONCLUSIONS: Associations between post-discharge thromboprophylaxis and outcomes differed across thoracic procedures and operative approaches. Favorable associations after esophagectomy contrasted with less consistent lung resection findings, supporting prospective studies to define procedure- and risk-specific prophylaxis strategies.
