title: Ischemic paralysis caused by internal iliac artery embolism after endovascular recanalization for lower extremity arteriosclerosis obliterans: a case report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Lower extremity paralysis is a devastating complication after endovascular therapy for lower extremity arteriosclerosis obliterans (LEAOD). Common mechanisms include ischemia-reperfusion injury, acute arterial embolism, and thrombosis. Paralysis caused by internal iliac artery embolism is exceptionally rare and may be overlooked when postoperative neurologic deficits are initially attributed to spinal or cerebral causes. CASE PRESENTATION: An 86-year-old man developed recurrent bilateral intermittent claudication 3 years after endovascular treatment for LEAOD, followed by right toe ulceration. Preoperative computed tomographic angiography showed severe multilevel stenosis and in-stent reocclusion in both lower limbs. He underwent bilateral thrombus aspiration, balloon angioplasty, and catheter-directed thrombolysis. One hour after the procedure, acute left lower limb weakness (muscle strength grade 0-1) and hypoesthesia below the mid-calf occurred. Emergency abdominal-pelvic non-contrast CT, lumbar spine MRI, brain imaging, and lower limb CTA excluded lumbar canal disease and stroke, while suggesting new internal iliac artery occlusion. Emergency thrombus aspiration and balloon angioplasty of the left internal iliac artery restored substantial patency and improved muscle strength to grade III-IV in the thigh and grade III in the leg. Because pain persisted and distal perfusion remained insufficient, femoral endarterectomy and infrapopliteal balloon angioplasty were subsequently performed. After 1 month of rehabilitation, muscle strength remained grade III, with persistent sensory impairment and assisted ambulation. CONCLUSIONS: Internal iliac artery embolism is a rare but clinically important cause of ischemic paralysis after peripheral endovascular intervention. In patients with extensive multilevel occlusive disease, preoperative assessment of internal iliac collateral perfusion and cautious staged procedural planning may reduce risk. Sudden postoperative limb paralysis should prompt urgent spinal and vascular imaging, followed by timely revascularization when ischemia is suspected.

title: Endovascular versus open repair for aortoiliac occlusive disease - nationwide in-hospital outcomes by sex.
abstract: Background: Patients and methods: Results: Conclusions Evidence comparing endovascular therapy and open surgery for aorto-iliac occlusive disease remains limited, particularly for early complications, resource use, and sex-specific outcomes.We conducted a retrospective nationwide cohort study using the 2023 German inpatient dataset. Adult hospitalisations with major endovascular or open aorto-iliac reconstructive procedures and arterial occlusive disease were included. Hospitalisations with aneurysm, dissection, or combined procedure codes were excluded. Outcomes included in-hospital mortality, myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), complications, length of stay, and reimbursement. Adjusted estimates were obtained employing a doubly robust estimator using machine learning algorithms and were stratified by sex.Among 2,710 hospitalisations, 1,923 (71.0%) underwent open surgery and 787 (29.0%) endovascular therapy; 41.3% involved women. Endovascular therapy was associated with lower adjusted risks of in-hospital mortality (RR .44, 95% CI .31-.64), MACCE (RR .47, 95% CI .34-.64), acute kidney injury (RR .38, 95% CI .29-.50), major bleeding (RR .36, 95% CI .25-.51), prolonged ventilation (RR .28, 95% CI .18-.43), and SAEs (RR .46, 95% CI .33-.65). Length of stay was shorter after endovascular therapy (-8.57 days, 95% CI -9.63 to -7.52), while reimbursement did not differ significantly. Sex-stratified estimates were more pronounced in men but exploratory without interaction testing.: Endovascular therapy was associated with lower in-hospital morbidity and mortality and shorter hospital stay than open surgery, with similar reimbursement. Case-based data lacked longitudinal follow-up and detailed clinical, anatomical and treatment-selection information, limiting causal and patient-level interpretation.

title: Long-Term Quantitative MRI and Quality-of-Life After Endovascular Therapy in Acute Ischemic Stroke - A MR CLEAN-NO IV Substudy.
abstract: 2 2 2 2 This study aims to explore the long-term evolution of endovascular treatment after acute ischemic stroke (AIS) using quantitative MRI, and its relationship with quality of life (QoL). In this long-term substudy of patients from the MR CLEAN-NO IV trial, patients were included who received 24-hour post-stroke MRI and were functionally independent 90 days after stroke onset. Patients underwent a quantitative MRI exam three years after stroke onset to measure focal volume loss, myelin damage, iron deposition, and atrophy within and around the ischemic lesion seen on 24-hour-MRI, in addition to a QoL assessment. Bayesian statistical analyses were used to assess MRI measures lateralized to the ipsilateral hemisphere and to evaluate the relationship of these measures with baseline and treatment characteristics along with QoL. The Bayes Factor (BF) reflected moderate, strong or very strong evidence (BF = 3.0;20;1.5⋅10respectively). In the 24 included patients, prominent focal volume loss, iron deposition, ventricular enlargement and myelin damage (BF:2.0⋅10) were observed peripheral to the initial 24-hour DWI lesion at long-term FU MRI. In the basal ganglia nuclei, very strong evidence of focal volume loss (BF > 8.1⋅10) and moderate to very strong evidence of iron deposition (BF: 5.0 to 2.7⋅10) were observed at long-term assessment. Higher systolic blood pressure was associated with reduced long-term ventricular atrophy (BF:5.8). Long-term differences in ipsilateral versus contralateral hippocampal volume difference (BF:8.0) and iron deposition (BF:4.1) were moderately associated with QoL. Long-term subtle yet widespread demyelination and iron deposition were observed, and these changes correlated with long-term recovery.

abstract: Chinese guideline for the laboratory diagnosis of venous thromboembolism 2026 edition Guiding Principles for the Formulation and Revision of Clinical Practice Guidelines in China (2022 Edition) Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a multifactorial disease induced by the interplay between environmental exposures and genetic predisposition. title: Progress on the related mechanisms of vascular calcification in autogenous arteriovenous fistula in hemodialysis patients.
abstract: Autologous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred vascular access for end-stage renal disease patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis as a replacement therapy. As the duration of dialysis increases, the risk of vascular access-related complications such as AVF stenosis, thrombosis, vascular calcification (VC), and aneurysm formation gradually rises. Among these, VC has been proven to be independently associated with the occurrence and mortality of cardiovascular diseases in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). VC in the AVF of dialysis patients can lead to AVF failure, severely limiting its usability and increasing the risk of mortality among dialysis patients. Unlike previous reviews that predominantly focused on isolated mechanisms such as mineral metabolism or arterial calcification, this narrative review innovatively integrates the crosstalk among hemodynamic stress, inflammation, oxidative stress, deficiency of endogenous calcification inhibitors and pathological matrix remodeling, thereby providing a multidimensional perspective on AVF-VC. This review reframes the current understanding of AVF-VC, shifting it from a generalized complication of CKD-mineral and bone disorder to a distinct, fistula-specific pathological entity. This conceptual advancement offers a theoretical foundation for developing precision intervention strategies tailored to the unique microenvironment of the AVF.

title: Beyond Patency: Patient-Centered Outcomes and the Proposed Accountability Gap in Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia.
abstract: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) carries 1-year mortality of 20% to 25%, comparable with many solid-organ malignancies. Technically successful revascularization, defined by anatomical patency, does not reliably deliver pain relief, restored function, or sustained quality of life. This narrative review synthesizes landmark randomized trials (BEST-CLI, BASIL-1, BASIL-2) and current European and United States guidelines, grading every claim with a scheme in which population indirectness downgrades design strength. We examine 4 domains of morbidity persisting after anatomically successful revascularization: mechanistically heterogeneous pain; functional and quality-of-life decline; psychological burden; and sustained health care use, including chronic opioid use (approximately 35%), unhealed wounds at 1 year (10%-32%), and unplanned 30-day readmission (approximately 25%). No patient-reported outcome measure has been validated specifically for CLTI or used as a co-primary trial endpoint. We propose an accountability gap: the under-measured transfer of unresolved morbidity from vascular services to primary care. We state it as a falsifiable prediction about the discrimination of patency rather than prevalence, with a pre-specified effect size, explicit treatment of death as a competing risk, and a core outcome battery justified against COSMIN criteria. Patient co-production is the indispensable next step.

title: Comparison of different interventions for promoting the maturation of autogenous arteriovenous fistula: A systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred access for patients undergoing hemodialysis. This study sought to identify the optimal intervention for promoting the maturation of AVFs through a network meta-analysis (NMA). METHODS: Cochrane Library, Embase, PubMed, and Web of Science databases were searched by computer for publications up to May 12, 2025, utilizing primary terms such as "arteriovenous fistula" and "maturation." Risk of bias was assessed utilizing the tool from the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews. Funnel plots and Egger's test were used to assess publication bias. Primary outcomes were the ultrasonographic and clinical maturation of AVFs. The secondary outcome was the vein diameter. An NMA was conducted employing a Bayesian random-effects or fixed-effects model. Mean differences (MD) and relative risks (RR) with 95% credible intervals (CrI) were calculated. Surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) values were utilized to rank different interventions. Analyses were performed using R 4.3.2. RESULTS: Finally, 11 RCTs involving 1202 patients were included. The studies encompassed a total of 5 interventions, namely isometric exercise (ISOM), isotonic exercise (ISOT), ISOM+ISOT, far infrared (FIR) therapy, and balloon-assisted maturation (BAM). The NMA revealed that compared with conventional care, ISOM ranked first in improving clinical maturation (RR = 1.4, 95% CrI: 1.2, 1.7, SUCRA = 98.07%) and ultrasonographic maturation (RR = 1.5, 95% CrI: 1.2, 1.8, SUCRA = 99.88%). ISOM+ISOT ranked first in increasing the diameter of the outflow vein (MD = 0.84, 95% CrI: 0.68, 1.0, SUCRA = 87.24%). CONCLUSION: n This study suggests that, among the evaluated interventions, ISOM has the highest probability of improving clinical maturation of AVFs based on moderate-certainty evidence, and evidence supporting its effect on ultrasonographic maturation is tentative given the limited sample size ( = 340). ISOM + ISOT demonstrated the greatest likelihood of effectively increasing vein diameter. These findings are probabilistic and require individualized application.

title: Preoperative levels of biomarkers of coagulation to predict massive bleeding after surgical repair for acute type A aortic dissection: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute type A aortic dissection is a highly emergent condition with a high mortality rate. The condition poses an imminent risk of serious complications such as coagulopathy with massive bleeding. This increases the risk of mortality even after surgical repair. Procoagulant drugs are routinely administered but some patients still suffer postoperative massive bleeding that can be fatal. The study aimed to investigate whether massive bleeding after surgical treatment for type A aortic dissection can be predicted preoperatively through routine coagulation tests such as APTT, PT (INR), fibrinogen, D-dimer, and platelets. METHODS: The study was a retrospective, single-center, cohort study performed at a tertiary cardiac surgery unit. A total of 474 patients who underwent surgery for type A aortic dissection at our department between January 2005 and May 2023 were included in the study. Of these, 87 patients had massive postoperative bleeding after surgery for type A aortic dissection and were compared to 387 patients who did not have massive postoperative bleeding. Uni- and multivariable analyses were performed using logistic regression. The multivariable model included predictors of massive bleeding. Bleeding-related routine lab variables were then forced into the model. RESULTS: 9 9 Patients with massive bleeding (18%) had higher preoperative activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) (33 s vs 29 s, p<0.01), and creatinine (97 µmol/L vs 87 µmol/L, p<0.01), as well as lower preoperative platelet counts (172 × 10/L vs 187 × 10/L, p=0.03) compared to patients without massive bleeding. Patients with massive bleeding also had longer duration of cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) (221 min vs 170 min, p<0.01) and suffered more postoperative complications. Multivariable logistic regression identified preoperative APTT per mmol increment (OR 1.04 (95% CI 1.01-1.07, p=0.01), preoperative APTT > 34.5 s (OR 2.95 (95% CI 1.60-5.47), p<0.01), preoperative creatinine > 82.5 µmol/L (OR 2.16 (95% CI 1.15-4.06), p=0.02), hypertension (OR 1.83 (95% CI 1.01-3.32), p<0.05) and CPB time per 10 min increment (OR 1.09 (95% CI 1.05-1.13, p<0.01)) as independent predictors of massive bleeding. CONCLUSION: Preoperative APTT exceeding 34.5 s was independently associated with massive bleeding after type A aortic dissection repair and may, pending prospective validation, help identify patients who could potentially benefit from earlier hemostatic intervention.

title: [Varicocele: comparison of minimally invasive treatment options : Endovascular embolization, microsurgery, and patient-tailored treatment selection].
abstract: BACKGROUND: Varicocele is the most common potentially treatable cause of male subfertility. Endovascular embolization is an established minimally invasive alternative to microsurgical ligation. OBJECTIVE: To place the indications, technique, outcomes, and limitations of varicocele embolization in context and to define its role relative to microsurgery. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Narrative, guideline- and evidence-based review of current WHO, EAU, AUA/ASRM, and CIRSE recommendations, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and relevant cohort studies published through July 2026. RESULTS: Treatment is primarily indicated in men with a palpable varicocele, abnormal semen parameters, and otherwise unexplained infertility; subclinical varicoceles and normal semen analyses do not justify intervention. Technical success of embolization is usually above 90% in experienced centers. Pregnancy rates are broadly similar to those after surgery, while overall morbidity tends to be lower. Recurrence may, however, be more frequent than after high ligation. No embolic agent has proved consistently superior. CONCLUSION: Varicocele embolization is an evidence-based alternative to surgery, particularly for recurrent disease, bilateral or complex venous anatomy, and when rapid recovery is a priority. Treatment should be selected through multidisciplinary, anatomy-based, and shared decision-making.

title: Conduction System Versus Right Ventricular Pacing in Patients Undergoing TAVR: A Multicenter Propensity-Matched Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pacemaker implantation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is common and has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Cardiac physiological pacing (CPP) may preserve ventricular synchrony and reduce heart failure (HF) events compared with right ventricular pacing (RVP). OBJECTIVES: This study sought to compare long-term clinical outcomes of CPP vs RVP in patients requiring permanent pacing after TAVR. METHODS: Registro de Estimulación Fisiológica-TAVR is a retrospective, multicenter nationwide registry including patients undergoing TAVR and pacemaker implantation within 30 days. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed using baseline clinical and echocardiographic variables, yielding 466 matched pairs. The primary endpoint was the composite of cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization. Cox proportional hazards models were used for time-to-event analyses. Median follow-up was 24 months. RESULTS: In the propensity score-matched cohort, CPP was associated with a lower incidence of the primary endpoint than RVP (9.7% vs 17.6%; HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.39-0.83; P = 0.003). This difference was driven by fewer HF hospitalizations (7.9% vs 13.9%; HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.37-0.86; P = 0.008). No significant differences were observed in cardiovascular death or all-cause mortality between groups. CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter propensity score-matched study, CPP after TAVR was associated with a lower risk of the primary endpoint, driven by fewer HF hospitalizations. These findings support the need for further randomized clinical trials to evaluate the role of CPP in post-TAVR patients requiring ventricular pacing.

title: Immediate Versus Staged Complete Revascularization in Multivessel Disease and STEMI: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
abstract: BACKGROUND: For patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and multivessel disease, complete revascularization is recommended. The timing of nonculprit lesion intervention, either immediately during the index procedure or staged at a later time, has been investigated in randomized controlled trials (RCTs). OBJECTIVES: This study sought to perform a meta-analysis of RCTs comparing immediate vs staged complete revascularization in patients with multivessel disease presenting with STEMI. METHODS: We conducted a frequentist, pairwise meta-analysis. Studies were selected based on the following inclusion criteria: multicenter RCTs comparing immediate vs staged nonculprit revascularization in patients presenting with STEMI; exclusive use of second-generation (or newer) drug-eluting stents; a follow-up duration of ≥1 year; and publication in a peer-reviewed journal. The primary outcome of interest was all-cause mortality, whereas secondary outcomes included myocardial infarction (MI), cardiac death, and unplanned revascularization. Summary estimates were computed using random-effects models with inverse-variance weighting based on trial-level HRs and 95% CIs. The study protocol was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251124207). RESULTS: 2 2 2 2 2 2 After a systematic search, 4 randomized trials comprising 2,651 patients were included in the meta-analysis. The risk of all-cause death at 1-year was higher with immediate complete revascularization (HR: 1.50; 95% CI: 1.02-2.21; P = 0.04; prediction interval [PI]: 0.80-2.81; I= 0%; t= 0). Immediate complete revascularization reduced the risk of recurrent MI when using the protocol specified definitions which included procedural MI (HR: 0.58; 95% CI: 0.36-0.94; P = 0.02; PI: 0.22-1.54; I= 0%; t= 0.034) but did not reduce risk of spontaneous MI (HR: 0.91; 95% CI: 0.55-1.48; P = 0.90; PI: 0.41-2.00; I= 0%; τ= 0.00). The risk of cardiac death and unplanned revascularization was comparable between the treatment groups. CONCLUSIONS: In STEMI and multivessel disease, immediate complete revascularization may be associated with an increased risk of all-cause death at 1-year when compared with staged complete revascularization. The treatment effect on mortality should be interpreted cautiously because of the relatively low number of deaths across the 4 trials and the statistical fragility of the findings. The findings from this analysis do not support an immediate complete revascularization strategy in these patients.

title: 1-Year Outcomes of Endovascular Repair of Zone 0/1 Aortic Arch Lesions with a Thoracic Branched Endoprosthesis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The GORE® TAG® Thoracic Branch Endoprosthesis (TBE) pivotal non-randomized, multicenter, prospective trial evaluated 1-year outcomes in patients at high risk for open surgical repair undergoing aortic arch and descending thoracic aorta endovascular repair (Zone 0/1). METHODS: Endpoints evaluated from endovascular procedure through 12 months included aortic-related death, disabling stroke, permanent paraplegia or paraparesis, new onset renal failure, and unanticipated reintervention. Core-lab identified endpoints included aortic rupture or enlargement (≥5 mm), Type I/III endoleak, device integrity, device migration, fistula, patency, and new dissection. RESULTS: The 77 enrolled patients had aneurysm (n=50), dissection (n=24), or other isolated lesion types (n=3); 90.9% had a Zone 0 proximal stent landing zone. Patients were a mean age of 70.8±10.8 years, 66.2% male, and 57.1% white and all had the aortic and side branch component implanted. Technical success was 94.8%. Early outcomes to 12 months included 8 (10.4%) aortic-related deaths, 6 (7.8%) disabling strokes (all aneurysm cohort), 4 (5.2%) unanticipated reintervention, 2 (2.6%) aortic ruptures, and 1 (1.3%) renal failure. Type IA/IB or Type III endoleaks occurred in 6 (7.8%) patients. Loss of side branch patency occurred in 1 (1.3%) patient. There was no permanent paraplegia or paraparesis or loss of device integrity or migration. A total of five patients had aortic enlargement; none required reintervention. CONCLUSIONS: Early data from this prospective investigation of the TBE device in Zone 0/1 applications signals that the device is a reasonable therapeutic alternative in patients with appropriate anatomy deemed high risk for open arch surgery.

title: Carotid stenosis reporting in Doppler ultrasound: why specifying NASCET or ECST criteria matters-an outpatient study.
abstract: PURPOSE: Carotid artery stenosis represents a major risk factor for ischemic stroke, and Doppler ultrasound is widely used as the first-line imaging modality for its assessment. The degree of stenosis is commonly expressed as a percentage and can be calculated according to different methods, most notably the North American Symptomatic Carotid Endarterectomy Trial (NASCET) and the European Carotid Surgery Trial (ECST) criteria. However, in routine clinical practice, the classification system used to determine the percentage of stenosis is not always specified in the ultrasound report. These methods consider different reference diameters, making values non-comparable and potentially misleading for clinical decisions. METHODS: In this study, we reviewed 1,400 patients evaluated in the Doppler ultrasound outpatient clinic of Internal Medicine at Poma Hospital, Mantova, Italy. All examinations were performed during routine clinical activity over four years by a physician tutor of the Italian Society of Medical and Biological Ultrasonology (SIUMB). The patient population included individuals aged between 18 and 97 years. RESULTS: During follow-up evaluations, it was frequently observed that previous ultrasound reports indicated a percentage of carotid stenosis without specifying whether NASCET or ECST criteria had been used. CONCLUSIONS: Our experience highlights the importance of clearly stating the classification system used for stenosis grading in carotid Doppler reports. Standardized reporting may improve longitudinal comparison of examinations, facilitate clinical decision-making, and enhance communication among healthcare professionals involved in the management of carotid artery disease.

title: The Importance of Family Centered Care and Cascade Screening in Patients with Heritable Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm Disease.
abstract: Heritable thoracic aortic aneurysm diseases (HTAAD) may be either syndromic or non-syndromic. While family screening for all forms of HTAAD has been recommended, providing care to an entire family is often fragmented in our siloed healthcare delivery model. We sought to determine the frequency of cascade family screening in the current era with either cardiovascular imaging (cascade cardiac screening) and/or genetic testing (cascade genetic screening), and to assess the impact of such testing on adverse outcomes in first degree family members. Of the 184 HTAAD patients who presented to our academic center without a known family history of aneurysmal disease, 84 were followed in a cardiology clinic, 40 in a genetics clinic and 60 in a combined cardiovascular genetics clinic for both children and adults. Cascade cardiac or genetic screening of ≥ 1 family member occurred during the course of care in 138 of 184 (75%) families. Complete cascade screening (genetic and/or cardiac) of all at-risk first-degree family members occurred in only 61 (33%) families and varied by clinic type (12%, 10% and 78%, p = 0.001) for those initially evaluated in a cardiology, genetics, or combined cardiovascular genetics clinic. As a result of cascade screening or an aortic event, 461 additional family members were identified as at risk for an aortic event. Of these, 53 family members from 42 families experienced an unexpected HTAAD-related event. Cascade screening was associated with a lower incidence of an event (1/53 vs. 52/53, p < 0.0001) during follow-up. Clinics that offer family-based care and on-site cascade screening facilitate timely diagnosis and intervention thereby reducing mortality from aortic disease.

title: Association of chronic kidney disease with major cardiovascular outcomes following lower extremity endovascular revascularization.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) amplifies cardiovascular risk, yet its stage-specific influence on perioperative outcomes following endovascular lower extremity revascularization (LER) for peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains poorly characterized. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the ACS NSQIP registry (2013-2022). Adults undergoing endovascular LER for PAD were stratified by preoperative estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) via the CKD-EPI 2021 equation: G1 (≥90), G2 (60-89), G3 (30-59), G4 (15-29), and G5 (<15 mL/min/1.73 m2 or dialysis dependent). The primary outcome was 30-day major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: myocardial infarction, stroke, or death). Multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). RESULTS: Among 22,424 patients (64.6% aged ≥65 years; 36.1% women), comorbidity burden increased progressively with CKD stage. Within 30 days, 556 patients (2.5%) experienced MACE. Event rates rose stepwise: 1.5% (G1), 1.6% (G2), 2.7% (G3), 4.9% (G4), and 6.0% (G5). After adjustment for age, sex, race/ethnicity, ASA class, admission status, presenting symptoms, and preoperative hematocrit, advanced CKD remained independently associated with MACE: OR 2.30 (95% CI 1.50-3.52) for G4 and OR 3.15 (95% CI 2.28-4.35) for G5 versus G1. CONCLUSION: CKD stage provides independent prognostic information in patients undergoing endovascular LER. Advanced CKD independently predicts 30-day MACE with a dose-response relationship across stages. Preoperative eGFR should be incorporated into perioperative risk stratification protocols to guide cardiovascular optimization and surveillance planning.

title: Circulatory arrest versus aortic cross-clamping in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm repair.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Aortic cross‑clamping and mild hypothermic circulatory arrest (MHCA) are commonly used strategies in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm surgery. This study compared these approaches in elective procedures for patients with a distal ascending aortic diameter of 40-50 mm. The primary outcome was a composite of 30‑day mortality, stroke, or acute kidney injury, with secondary outcomes including long‑term survival and postoperative complications. MATERIAL AND METHODS: n n This single‑center observational cohort included patients treated between 2016 and 2024. Distal ascending aortic diameters were assessed on preoperative computed tomography, and clinical data were obtained from SWEDEHEART. Patients were assigned to aortic cross‑clamp ( = 261) or MHCA ( = 138). Propensity score matching was performed in a 1:1 ratio to balance baseline characteristics. RESULTS: p p The composite primary outcome occurred in 15 patients (3.8%) and was more common with MHCA than with cross‑clamp (6.5% vs 2.3%, = 0.035). Two patients (0.5%), both in the MHCA group, died within 30 days. After matching, the odds ratio for the composite endpoint was 2.4 (95% CI, 0.66-11.5), indicating no significant difference. Long‑term survival was similar between groups (log‑rank = 0.33). CONCLUSIONS: Both strategies were associated with low perioperative risk and comparable long‑term survival. These results support flexible operative planning, allowing the distal anastomotic technique to be chosen based on individual anatomy and surgical preference.

title: Estrogen hormonal therapy is not associated with increased risk of venous thrombosis in total hip arthroplasty or hemiarthroplasty for femoral neck fractures.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of estrogen hormone therapy on venous thrombotic events for femoral neck fractures treated with either total hip arthroplasty (THA) or hemiarthroplasty (HA). DESIGN: Retrospective cohort analysis. SETTING: TriNetX Health Research Network. PATIENT SELECTION CRITERIA: Patients who sustained a femoral neck fracture (OTA/AO 31B) between 2005 and 2025 who were treated with either THA or HA were categorized into groups based on whether they were prescribed systemic estrogen hormone therapy (EHT) within 3 months before or after their fracture. OUTCOME MEASURES AND COMPARISONS: The primary outcomes were deep vein thrombosis (DVT) or pulmonary embolism (PE) within 3 months after their fracture. A matched cohort was created after a 1:1 propensity match for demographics, diabetes, obesity, and tobacco use. Measures of association models were used to determine odds ratios. RESULTS: P P A total of 39,631 patients with femoral neck fractures treated with either a THA or HA were identified. Of these, 330 (0.8%) patients with femoral neck fractures were prescribed estrogen within 3 months before or after their fracture. After a matched cohort comparison, there were no statistically significant differences in rates of PE (odds ratio [OR] = 1.31; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.56-3.03;= 0.525) or for DVT (OR = 1.67; 95% CI, 0.78-3.61;= 0.184). CONCLUSION: Systemic EHT was not associated with a significantly increased risk of DVT or PE after operatively treated femoral neck fractures with THA or HA. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, Prognostic.

title: Functional connectivity recovers canine-human network homology along the evolutionary cortical hierarchy.
abstract: ≈ p = 0.002 p > 0.3 p = 0.93 Mapping functional brain organization between species is a prerequisite for translating connectivity biomarkers from animal models to patients, but connectivity-based correspondence has been demonstrated almost exclusively in primates. We tested whether canine-human network homology can be recovered from functional connectivity alone, using only five network-level anatomical priors, and benchmarked a spectral manifold alignment framework (Laplacian-eigenmap embedding with Procrustes alignment on network centroids) against a simple connectivity-signature matching baseline. Data comprised resting-state fMRI from 15 canines with endovascular permanent middle cerebral artery occlusion (pre-occlusion baseline and hyperacute post-occlusion sessions) and two public OpenNeuro datasets: 29 chronic-phase post-stroke aphasia patients scanned before and after rehabilitation (ds003999) and 10 healthy controls (ds000224). Held-out canine-human network homologies were recovered well above chance (top-5 network correspondence up to 54.5% vs. permutation null18%,), and correspondence followed the evolutionary cortical hierarchy: visual and somatomotor homologies were recovered several-fold above chance, default-mode only weakly-extending a gradient previously described in primates to a carnivore. Notably, simple signature matching (54.5%) outperformed manifold alignment (35.5%), indicating that the homology signal is strong enough to be captured without embedding machinery at translational cohort sizes. Within species, canine network metrics showed no treatment-arm differences (all), and chronic-phase patients did not differ from controls in modularity (); a sensitivity analysis bounds these nulls. All results are fully reproducible from shared code and public data.

title: A meta-analysis of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt with or without embolization for esophageal and gastric variceal bleeding in decompensated liver cirrhosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate whether transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) combined with embolization could further improve efficacy for patients with decompensated liver cirrhosis complicated with esophageal and gastric variceal bleeding. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and Cochrane Library, for all relevant randomized controlled trials and cohort studies up to March 2025. Statistical results were evaluated using risk ratios and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: A total of 14 studies involving 3079 patients were included. The statistical results showed that the rebleeding rate in the TIPS combined with embolization group was lower than that in the TIPS alone group (risk ratios = 0.67; 95% CI = 0.57-0.79; P  < 0.001), and the same result was observed only in the subgroup of patients with gastric variceal bleeding (risk ratios = 0.50; 95% CI = 0.34-0.74; P  < 0.001). There was no significant difference between the groups in patients with isolated esophageal variceal bleeding (risk ratios = 0.83; 95% CI = 0.51-1.35; P  = 0.46). In addition, the incidence of hepatic encephalopathy in the TIPS combined with embolization group was also lower than that in the TIPS alone group (risk ratios = 0.82; 95% CI = 0.73-0.91; P  < 0.001), but there was no significant difference in survival rate (risk ratios = 1.00; 95% CI = 0.97-1.03; P  = 0.94). CONCLUSION: Compared with TIPS alone, the combined treatment showed a trend toward lower rebleeding and hepatic encephalopathy, yet survival appeared similar between the two groups.

title: Meta-analysis of the histopathological features of surgically removed aortas classified according to the SCVP and AECVP consensus documents.
abstract: The Society for Cardiovascular Pathology (SCVP) and the Association for European Cardiovascular Pathology (AECVP) published consensus statements on the surgical pathology of the aorta to unify nomenclature and provide a new classification scheme to systematically evaluate the degenerative and inflammatory lesions of the thoracic aorta. The aim of this meta-analysis was to determine the histopathological features of thoracic aneurysmatic aortas, thoracic dissected aortas, and thoracic aortas in patients with a bicuspid aortic valve (BAV). Additionally, the aim was to map how consensus documents and classification schemes is used in practice and research. Articles for analysis were identified while searching for references to the SCVP and AECVP consensus documents, resulting in 174 articles. After applying the exclusion and inclusion criteria, 10 articles were included in the analysis. Four cohorts were analysed: the whole cohort, the aneurysm cohort, the dissection cohort, and the BAV cohort. Medial degeneration was found in all cohorts. The dissection cohort showed more severe medial degeneration than the aneurysm cohort or the BAV cohort. The BAV cohort showed the mildest medial degeneration compared to the other cohorts. More prevalent smooth muscle cell nuclei loss was linked to dissection. The BAV cohort showed milder changes in elastic fibers. Atherosclerosis was comparable among all cohorts. Medial degeneration represents the pathological process of several aortic diseases. All studied components of medial degeneration were present in aneurysms, dissections, and BAV aortas. The consensus documents have been useful tools and assist with the systematic evaluation of resected aortas, although their use in the complexity is limited.

title: Infective endocarditis after transcatheter aortic valve implantation - data from national registry.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: There is relatively little detailed information about patients with IE after TAVI from nationwide registries. AIM: To evaluate the incidence of IE after TAVI, to analyse the characteristics of patients, infectious agents, type of IE and patients' outcomes. METHODS: A total of 9887 TAVIs were performed at 14 centres in the Czech Republic between 2010 and 2023. Rehospitalization for potential IE (according to ICD-10 diagnosis) were identified. A total of 129 patients were confirmed with IE (27× possible IE, 102× definite IE) with cumulative incidence of 1.3%. The TAVI prosthesis in patients with definite IE was affected in 71 patients (70%), IE on mitral valve was present in 22 patients, 7 patients had device IE and site of infection was not identified in 2 patients. The main infectious agents were Enterococcus faecalis (37 patients, 29%) and Staphylococcus aureus (28 patients, 21%). Streptococcus species were the causative agents of IE in 27 cases (21%). Time from TAVI to occurrence of IE did not differ among the four main microbiological groups. The in-hospital mortality rate of patients with confirmed IE was 27%. CONCLUSION: The cumulative incidence of infective endocarditis after TAVI was 1.3% in the large nationwide registry, with an in-hospital mortality of 27%. Enterococcus species were the most common pathogens without differences in time distribution compared to other causative agents.

title: Single-stage hybrid repair of extensive aortic dissection with traumatic diaphragmatic hernia.
abstract: We report a rare case of a 70-year-old male patient who developed a left diaphragmatic hernia combined with extensive aortic dissection and exhibited signs of lower limb ischemia following a motor vehicle accident. An urgent, single-stage surgical intervention was performed, consisting of endovascular aortic repair first to stabilize circulation, followed by diaphragmatic repair. The patient recovered smoothly postoperatively, with no abnormalities observed at 1-month and 6-month follow-ups. This case highlights the necessity of accurate diagnosis and multidisciplinary team collaboration in emergency thoracoabdominal trauma.

title: Effect of fenofibrate on diabetic retinopathy progression: an RCT-Only systematic review and meta-analysis incorporating the LENS trial.
abstract: 2 Diabetic retinopathy (DR) causes preventable vision loss, yet treatments remain reactive. Fenofibrate showed ophthalmic benefits in cardiovascular trials, and LENS (2024) expanded the evidence. Under a pre-registered PRISMA 2020 protocol we searched four databases to June 25, 2026 for randomized trials of fenofibrate reporting an ophthalmic outcome in adults with diabetes, applied RoB 2 and GRADE, and pooled dichotomous outcomes as random-effects risk ratios (RR). Ten studies met inclusion criteria: six completed with extractable results and four ongoing; three completed trials contributed to the primary pooled outcome. All enrolled predominantly type 2 diabetes (one trial 26% type 1, no type-specific estimate). For DR progression, three trials (N = 3,756) gave RR 0.77 (95% CI 0.68-0.88;HKSJ 0.60-0.99; I0%; moderate certainty), 45 fewer events per 1,000; stratification gave 0.80 (0.68-0.93) for the LENS composite and 0.70 (0.55-0.90) for ETDRS step-based definitions (difference P = 0.37). Need for retinal treatment fell under the conventional model (RR 0.68, 0.57-0.82) but at low certainty: 90.2% of the weight came from one pre-anti-VEGF-era trial and the HKSJ interval crossed the null (0.42-1.11), so this outcome is not firm evidence about contemporary treatment need. No trial found benefit for visual acuity or function (low certainty); macular edema evidence was not combinable (very low certainty). Venous thromboembolism was increased (RR 1.52, 1.12-2.06), an estimate derived entirely from FIELD (103/4,755 vs 68/4,767). In adults with diabetes, predominantly type 2, fenofibrate slows structural DR progression but is not established as vision-preserving.

title: Endovascular therapy for mild-to-moderate stroke due to basilar artery occlusion: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Endovascular therapy (EVT) is an established treatment for basilar artery occlusion (BAO) with severe deficits, but its benefit in patients with mild-to-moderate symptoms (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] <10) remains unclear due to limited randomized controlled trial (RCT) evidence. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate EVT efficacy and safety in this subgroup. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library for RCTs and observational studies published between January 1, 2014, and July 1, 2026, comparing EVT plus best medical treatment (BMT) versus BMT in BAO with NIHSS <10. The primary outcome was 90-day good functional status (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-2). Secondary outcomes were favorable (mRS 0-3) and excellent (mRS 0-1) functional status. Safety outcomes included 90-day mortality, any intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and symptomatic ICH. RESULTS: Fifteen studies comprising 3981 patients (1812 EVT; 2169 BMT) were included. No significant differences were observed in good (OR = 1.51; 95% CI 0.89-2.54; p = 0.12) or favorable functional status (OR = 0.99; 95% CI 0.75-1.30; p = 0.92), while EVT increased the odds of excellent status (OR = 2.01; 95% CI 1.33-3.05; p < 0.001). Mortality (OR = 0.94; 95% CI 0.55-1.59), any ICH (OR = 1.23; 95% CI 0.69-2.19) and symptomatic ICH (OR = 0.98; 95% CI 0.61-1.57) were comparable. CONCLUSION: Although no difference emerged for the primary outcome, EVT increased the likelihood of excellent recovery without compromising safety. These findings highlight the need for RCTs targeting this population.

title: The role of anti-factor Xa in patients with cancer receiving prophylactic low-molecular-weight heparin: a meta-analysis.
abstract: I I I 2 2 2 Low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) is a mainstay in the prevention of cancer-associated thrombosis. However, there is a lack of clear guidelines around routine monitoring of anti-factor Xa (AFXa) levels in patients with cancer receiving LMWH for prophylaxis. This study compares fixed vs laboratory-based dosing of LMWH in patients with cancer to elucidate if there are significant differences in venous thromboembolism (VTE) and bleeding outcomes for this population. To our knowledge, this is the first meta-analysis that evaluates AFXa monitoring, specifically in patients with cancer. A total of 561 articles were screened, and 5 studies were included in the meta-analysis. Two studies directly compared outcomes of fixed dosing vs AFXa-based dosing, and 4 studies evaluated outcomes based on whether AFXa values were subprophylactic, prophylactic, or supraprophylactic. The relative risk (RR) of VTE was higher in fixed dosing vs adjusting for AFXa levels, although this failed to reach statistical significance (RR, 9.27; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.90-95.29;= 0.0%). Surprisingly, patients with subprophylactic AFXa levels experienced bleeding events at 6% (95% CI, 0.00-0.24;= 73.3%) compared to 2% at prophylactic levels (95% CI, 0.00-0.08;= 3.1%), although the difference was not statistically significant. Our findings suggest a lack of benefit in monitoring AFXa in prophylaxis for preventing VTE; however, further investigation into high-risk malignancies or patients undergoing cancer surgery may elucidate differences in VTE and bleeding outcomes that guide future prophylactic anticoagulation.

title: SHR-2004, a Humanized Monoclonal Antibody Targeting Factor XI, for Preventing Venous Thromboembolism After Ovarian Cancer Surgery: A Randomized, Active-Controlled Phase 2 Study.
abstract: This multicenter, randomized, open-label, exploratory Phase 2 trial assessed SHR-2004, an anti-FXI antibody, for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prevention in patients undergoing ovarian cancer surgery-a population at particularly high thrombotic risk conducted at 25 sites in China. Patients with newly diagnosed Stage III-IV or recurrent ovarian cancer scheduled for surgery were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive subcutaneous SHR-2004 (180 mg on Day 1 and 120 mg on Day 15) or enoxaparin-rivaroxaban (subcutaneous enoxaparin 40 mg once daily during hospitalization, followed by oral rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily after discharge until Day 28). The primary efficacy outcome was the composite of VTE events within 28 days. The primary safety outcome was major bleeding (MB) or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding (CRNMB) from first dose to 28 days. Between February 19, 2024 and September 17, 2024, 198 patients received assigned treatment (90 with SHR-2004, 108 with enoxaparin-rivaroxaban) and were included in the safety analysis. Among 181 patients who completed protocol-mandated ultrasonography, VTE occurred in 11 (12.6%) patients in the SHR-2004 group and 19 (20.2%) in the enoxaparin-rivaroxaban group (difference -8.4%, 95% CI -19.9 to 3.1) by Day 28. MB/CRNMB rates were similar between groups (SHR-2004: 2/90 [2.2%]; enoxaparin-rivaroxaban: 2/108 [1.9%]). In this study, SHR-2004 showed comparable efficacy to enoxaparin-rivaroxaban for preventing postoperative VTE in patients undergoing ovarian cancer surgery, with a similar low risk of MB or CRNMB. The twice-monthly dosing schedule offers a potential advantage over daily anticoagulation, supporting further investigation in adequately powered Phase 3 trials. title: Effects of Sarpogrelate Versus Aspirin on Whole Blood Viscosity in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Peripheral Artery Disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Whole blood viscosity (WBV) is associated with impaired microvascular circulation and cardiovascular risk in patients with Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and peripheral artery disease (PAD). This study investigated the efficacy and safety of sarpogrelate compared with aspirin on WBV in patients with T2DM and PAD. METHODS: -1 This randomised, open-label clinical trial enrolled adults with T2DM and PAD. A total of 66 participants were randomised to aspirin (n = 33) or sarpogrelate (n = 33) for 24 weeks. The primary endpoint was change in diastolic WBV at a shear rate of 1 sfrom baseline to week 24. Secondary endpoints included tissue oxygen delivery index, pain visual analogue scale (VAS) and cold sensation scores. RESULTS: After 24 weeks, diastolic WBV did not decrease significantly in both groups (sarpogrelate group: 31.91 ± 7.83 to 30.76 ± 7.08, mean change, -1.15 ± 9.25; p = 0.509; aspirin group: 33.32 ± 8.86 to 32.12 ± 9.60, mean change, -1.20 ± 8.36; p = 0.432). VAS scores improved significantly in both groups (mean change, -9.09 ± 18.09; p = 0.007 for sarpogrelate; -6.13 ± 16.47; p = 0.047 for aspirin), with no between-group difference. Cold sensation scores improved only in the sarpogrelate group (mean change, -0.21 ± 0.55; p = 0.033 vs. -0.23 ± 0.85; p = 0.147 for aspirin group), with no between-group difference. CONCLUSION: In patients with T2DM and PAD, sarpogrelate did not significantly improve WBV compared with aspirin. VAS scores and cold sensation improved significantly within the sarpogrelate group with no between-group difference.

title: Clinically Relevant Outcomes With Romiplostim in Patients With Solid Tumors and Persistent Chemotherapy Induced Thrombocytopenia.
abstract: Thrombopoietin receptor agonists (TPO-RAs), such as romiplostim, are commonly utilized to facilitate timely platelet recovery and administration of chemotherapy in patients with cancer and chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia (CIT). However, there are limited data on the effect of TPO-RAs on clinically important outcomes. A target trial emulation study was implemented to assess the effects of romiplostim in patients with solid tumors and persistent CIT, compared to controls. Patients were exact-matched on chemotherapy, cancer type, degree of thrombocytopenia, and 1:1 propensity-score-matched on clinical/laboratory variables on Day 1 of romiplostim treatment or quasi-index date for controls. Study outcomes included overall survival over 24 months and venous thromboembolism (VTE) at 6 months. This study included 165 romiplostim-treated patients and 165 controls. Baseline characteristics were well-balanced. The median age was 61 years and 52% were female. The median romiplostim duration was 1.38 months. Median overall survival was 13 months (95% CI: 9.9-23) in the romiplostim group and 9.5 months (95% CI: 7.1-14.0) in controls (hazard ratio [HR] 0.86 [95% CI: 0.65-1.13]). There was a numerical improvement in survival with romiplostim (0.80 [95% CI: 0.60-1.06]) which was statistically significant in the subgroup of patients with metastatic disease (HR 0.70 [95% CI: 0.52-0.95]). The 6-month cumulative incidence of VTE was 10.0% (95% CI: 6.3%-16.0%) in the romiplostim group and 8.0% (95% CI: 4.5%-13.0%) in controls (HR 1.31 [95% CI: 0.64-2.70]), with death as a competing risk. In conclusion, these results support the safety of romiplostim in CIT with observed numerical improvement in overall survival at 2 years.

title: Machine learning-derived serum carbon dioxide trajectories in predicting prognosis of patients with acute aortic dissection.
abstract: Venous partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PvCO 2 ) indicates postoperative adverse outcomes in patients with acute aortic dissection, and its trajectories over time affecting postoperative adverse outcomes remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between PvCO 2 trajectories and postoperative adverse outcomes, as well as clinical application through group-based trajectory modeling and machine-learning algorithms. This retrospective cohort study analyzed data from 642 patients with acute aortic dissection treated at the Fourth Hospital of Hebei Medical University from 2019 to 2024, to determine postoperative adverse outcomes, including 6-month mortality and complications. Three PvCO 2 tests within the first 72 hours of admission were used to analyze PvCO 2 trajectories through group-based trajectory modeling. To diagnose high-risk PvCO 2 trajectories in emergency settings, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression was conducted to select key features, which were consequently integrated into predictive models using multiple machine-learning methods. Finally, a web-based interpretable website was developed for predicting PvCO 2 trajectories in patients with acute aortic dissection. Overall, 642 patients were classed into four PvCO 2 trajectories (T1, persistent decrease from a medium to a low level; T2, stable low level; T3, persistent decrease from a high to a low level; T4, stable midlevel), showing distinct patterns. After adjustment for other covariates, postoperative adverse outcomes among these groups showed significant differences, with a higher proportion of postoperative adverse outcomes in the T3 group. Subsequently, upon Shapley additive explanations analysis, 17 features with importance sequence were identified (hemoglobin, direct bilirubin, monocyte, adenosine deaminase, drinking, anion gap, chloride, platelet, lymphocyte, albumin/globulin ratio, calcium, alanine aminotransferase, α-L-fucosidase, D-dimer, antihypertensive drugs, and smoking), which were integrated into the model for predicting T3. The optimal machine-learning model was established for predicting postoperative adverse outcomes. Finally, a web-based interpretable model was developed to predict patients with acute aortic dissection and high risk of postoperative adverse outcomes. This study uncovers heterogeneity in PvCO 2 trajectory, highlighting that decreased PvCO 2 is associated with worse prognosis. A web-based tool for the prediction of acute aortic dissection patients at high risk of postoperative adverse outcomes was constructed to facilitate clinical application.

title: Durability of a physician-modified endograft constructed using the Terumo Aortic TREO device: A postmortem evaluation.
abstract: Fenestrated endovascular repair using physician-modified endografts has become an important treatment option for complex abdominal aortic aneurysms, although long-term graft durability data remain limited. We present a unique postmortem evaluation of a physician-modified endograft implanted for a juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm as part of an Investigational Device Exemption trial (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT01538056). Postmortem examination demonstrated no evidence of stent fracture, graft migration, or structural failure. The graft remained well incorporated within the aortic neck with preserved fixation and seal. These findings provide the first reported human postmortem evidence supporting the durability of a physician-modified Terumo Aortic TREO endograft.

title: Sex- and Age-specific Outcomes After Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (RAAA) remains a medical catastrophe. Although early outcomes improved, contemporary data integrating early and long-term survival, and postdischarge care needs across sex- and age groups is limited. METHODS: This nationwide cohort included Dutch RAAA repairs between 2014 and 2023. Dutch Surgical Aneurysm Audit data were linked to Statistics Netherlands registries. Outcomes included 90-day mortality, long-term survival, and postdischarge care. RESULTS: Of the 3642 patients, 15.2% were women, who were older (76.3 vs. 74.0 y) and more often required open repair (61.4% vs. 54.0%). Ninety-day mortality increased with age and was higher in women (39.1% vs. 29.1%), but female sex was not independently associated with early mortality after adjustment.Among 90-day survivors, absolute long-term survival was similar, but relative survival was lower in women (5-year relative survival 68.0% vs. 78.3%). Women were less often discharged home (42.4% vs. 56.7%) and more frequently required early homecare (47.7% vs. 34.7%). Reinterventions were more common after EVAR than open repair and occurred less frequently in women. CONCLUSION: In this nationwide linked audit-registry analysis, outcomes after RAAA repair improved substantially, despite lower estimated in-hospital turndown rates than in earlier eras. The higher early mortality in women WAS reflected by differences in age, presentation severity, and repair type - possibly reflecting less favorable aneurysm anatomy. Female sex also associated with an increased long-term excess mortality and greater postdischarge dependency. These findings indicate that optimization of care for women with a RAAA is not confined to perioperative mortality, but extends across the entire care pathway.

title: Key factors for predicting outcomes one year after Meso-Rex bypass surgery and optimizing the surgical plan in children with extrahepatic portal vein obstruction.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To analyze the factors for predicting 1-year outcomes and optimize surgical planning for Meso-Rex bypass (MRB) in children with extrahepatic portal vein obstruction (EHPVO). MATERIALS AND METHODS: From October 2014 to July 2024, children with EHPVO after MRB were retrospectively analyzed. The number of MRB, the type of bypass vessel, and the position of the lower anastomosis were collected. Predictive variables include the diameter of the connection between the left and right portal veins, the Rex vein (RV) diameter, the number of RV branches, the diameter of the thickest RV branch, and the bypass-to-superior mesenteric vein (SMV) angle, which were measured by Contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) one week after MRB. The upper and lower anastomotic stenosis were diagnosed by Ultrasound and CECT one year after MRB. RESULTS: A total of 153 children (median age 72 months, 87 males) were included in this study. Univariate factors include the number of MRBs, the type of bypass vessel, and CECT variables (except the diameter of the thickest RV branch). Numbers of MRB and RV branches were retained in the final model for upper anastomotic stenosis. The combination of MRB > 1 and RV branches ≤ 4 predicts it post-MRB with 75% sensitivity, 86.4% specificity, and an area under the receiver operator characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.832. The bypass-to-SMV angle ≤ 110° predicts lower anastomotic stenosis after MRB with 90% sensitivity, 73.39% specificity, and AUC 0.847. CONCLUSIONS: Associated factors are useful for early postoperative risk stratification. Moreover, the type of bypass vessel and the bypass-to-SMV angle could be used to inform future surgical technique refinement. FindingsAssociated factors include bypass-to-SMV angle, number of MRB, RV branches and diameter, left-right portal vein connection diameter, and type of bypass vessel. Clinical RelevanceAssociated factors are useful for early postoperative risk stratification. Moreover, the internal jugular vein as the bridge vessel and the bypass-to-SMV angle > 110° could be used to optimize the surgical plan for a better outcome.

title: Efficacy and safety of revascularization in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia by kidney function.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The optimal revascularization strategy for patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) with chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains unknown. We evaluated whether the efficacy and safety of surgical vs endovascular revascularization differ by kidney function. METHODS: In this post hoc secondary analysis of BEST-CLI trial (NCT02060630), 1,704 patients with CLTI were stratified by baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR, mL/min/1.73 m²): non-CKD (eGFR ≥ 90), mild-moderate CKD (eGFR 45-89), advanced CKD (eGFR < 45 or dialysis). The primary outcome was a composite of major adverse limb events (MALE) or death. We estimated the difference in restricted mean time lost (RMTL, in days) adjusted for inverse probability treatment weights. RESULTS: Surgical revascularization was significantly associated with fewer days with MALE or death in non-CKD (RMTL difference: -127.8 days; 95% CI -176.1, -79.6) and mild-moderate CKD (-63.2 days; 95% CI -104.7, -21.8) but not in advanced CKD (-16.4 days; 95% CI -78.8, 46.0; P interaction = .02). This attenuation reflected a diminishing mortality benefit with more severe CKD (P interaction = .01), whereas the association with fewer days with MALE remained consistent across CKD strata (P interaction = .34). Major adverse cardiovascular events and serious adverse events were more common with more severe CKD but did not differ significantly by treatment. CONCLUSIONS: Surgical vs endovascular revascularization was consistently associated with fewer days with MALE across CKD strata. However, its association with mortality varied by kidney function, attenuating the overall benefit for the composite endpoint of MALE or death. These results support individualized revascularization strategies, but require prospective confirmation. TRIAL REGISTRATION: The BEST CLI trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT02060630).

title: Premature peripheral arterial disease is associated with worse outcomes after endovascular peripheral vascular intervention.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Premature peripheral arterial disease (PAD), defined as onset before the age of 50 years, is increasing in prevalence. The clinical characteristics, treatment patterns, and mid- and late-term outcomes of patients with premature PAD undergoing endovascular peripheral vascular intervention (PVI) are not well-defined. METHODS: The linked Vascular Quality Initiative and Medicare dataset was used to examine those who underwent PVI for arterial occlusive disease from January 2017 to December 2018. The exclusion criteria were acute limb ischemia and concomitant open revascularization. Patient demographics, operative characteristics, and outcomes were analyzed by group: premature versus nonpremature PAD. The primary outcomes of interest included risk of major amputation and 30-day, 90-day, and 1-year mortality. Time-to-event analyses were employed to calculate the cumulative incidence and derive the risk between the groups for the primary outcomes. RESULTS: A total of 15,050 patients were identified: 14,699 with nonpremature PAD (97.7%) and 351 with premature (2.3%). The premature PAD group had a higher proportion of women (49.0% vs 41.2%; P = .003), higher proportion of minoritized group members, and higher comorbidity burden. The premature PAD group commonly presented with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (79.8% vs 60.3%; P < .001) and prior amputation, both minor (21.4% vs 8.4%; P < .001) and major (19.1% vs 8.7%; P < .001). Patients with premature PAD had a significantly higher cumulative incidence of major amputation at 30 days (4.6% vs 1.9%; P = .006), 90 days (13.7% vs 5.2%; P < .001), and 1 year (21.9% vs 8.9%; P < .001), with a significantly shorter mean time-to-amputation than that of their nonpremature PAD counterparts (14.6 [10.5] vs 17.3 [10.3] months; P < .001). Despite the significant difference in the mean age between the groups (28.3 [4.6] years), no significant difference was noted in 30-day, 90-day, or 1-year all-cause mortality, with a similar mean time-to-death, between the premature and nonpremature PAD groups (18.2 vs 18.6 months; P = .52). In multivariable analysis, premature PAD was not associated with mortality at 30 days (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 0.93; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.49-1.75; P = .82), 90 days (aHR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.63-1.40; P = .76), or 1 year (aHR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.64-1.07; P = .15). However, premature PAD remained independently associated with 90-day (aHR, 1.62; 95% CI, 1.20-2.19; P < .001) and 1-year major amputation (aHR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.24-1.99; P < .0001). CONCLUSIONS: Patients with premature PAD undergoing PVI represent a high-risk population characterized by higher comorbidity burden, advanced disease at presentation, significantly higher 1-year major amputation rates, and comparable mortality to patients with nonpremature PAD despite an almost 30-year difference in the mean age between the groups. Further work should focus on identifying the barriers to optimal medical therapy and developing targeted intervention strategies to mitigate limb loss in this vulnerable cohort.

title: Omega-3 fatty acids, specialized pro-resolving mediators, and depression: A mechanistic meta-analysis of precursors and clinical implications.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (n-3 PUFAs), especially eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), exhibit adjunctive antidepressant efficacy despite negligible detectable levels in the brain. Emerging evidence implicates specialized pro‑resolving mediators (SPMs); bioactive n-3 PUFA metabolites offer a coherent pathway by actively resolving inflammation, enhancing tissue repair, and supporting neuronal function. To test whether n‑3 PUFA supplementation activates pro‑resolving biology in humans, this meta‑analysis quantified effects on circulating SPM precursors. METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, GOED, and the Cochrane Library (up to May 18, 2026) to identify RCTs examining the impact of n-3 PUFAs supplementation on circulating SPM precursors 18-hydroxyeicosapentaenoic acid (18-HEPE) and 17-hydroxydocosahexaenoic acid (17-HDHA). Meta-analysis was performed using Review Manager 5.4.1 with random-effects models. RESULTS: Eleven RCTs, comprising 810 participants, were included. N-3 PUFAs supplementation significantly and robustly increased the concentrations of both circulating SPM precursors: 18-HEPE (SMD = 1.05, 95% CI 0.54-1.55, Z = 4.08, P = 0.0001) and 17-HDHA (SMD = 0.69, 95% CI 0.19-1.18, Z = 2.72, P = 0.006). Importantly, subgroup analyses revealed that this increase was selectively amplified in patient populations characterized by a significant inflammatory, metabolic, and oxidative burden, including peripheral artery disease (PAD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), MDD with comorbid obesity, and pregnancy, but was negligible in healthy infants. CONCLUSION: N-3 PUFA supplementation significantly increased circulating 18-HEPE and 17-HDHA, indicating greater availability of upstream EPA- and DHA-derived SPM precursors across mixed human populations. However, whether these precursor changes translate into increased downstream SPM production or clinical antidepressant effects remains uncertain and requires dedicated trials in MDD populations. title: Hospital volume and vascular surgery specialization are associated with in-hospital mortality after invasive treatment of type B aortic dissection.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Type B aortic dissection (TBAD) requires complex surgical or endovascular treatment in a subset of patients. Whether the hospital caseload or vascular surgery specialization affects perioperative outcomes remains unclear. This study evaluated the association of annual hospital volume and vascular surgery specialization with in-hospital mortality after TBAD treatment in Germany. METHODS: We performed a nationwide retrospective analysis of German Diagnosis-Related Group hospital episode data from 2010 to 2023. All patients surgically or endovascularly treated for TBAD were identified using International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision, German Modification and procedural (Operations and Procedures Code) codes. Hospitals were stratified into four annual caseload categories (≤5, 6-10, 11-20, and >20 cases). The primary outcome was the in-hospital mortality rate; the secondary outcomes included major perioperative complications. Multilevel logistic regression (random intercepts for hospital and year) was performed to assess the association of the hospital volume and vascular surgery specialization of the treating surgeon with mortality, with adjustment for demographics, comorbidities, and treatment modality. RESULTS: A total of 18,400 patients with treated TBAD were identified. Very-high-volume hospitals (>20 cases/year) treated 36.9% of all patients, and low-volume hospitals (≤5 cases/year) accounted for 67.4% of the treating institutions but only for 22.3% of the procedures. Overall, the in-hospital mortality rate was 9.1%, decreasing from 10.1% in low-volume to 7.8% in very-high-volume hospitals. In risk-adjusted analyses, low- and medium-volume hospitals had significantly higher in-hospital mortality rates (odds ratio [OR], 1.30; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.05-1.60; P = .016 and OR, 1.32; 95% CI, 1.06-1.64; P = .013, respectively, vs very-high-volume hospitals), and treatment in vascular surgery departments was associated with reduced in-hospital mortality (OR, 0.44; 95% CI, 0.36-0.54; P < .001). CONCLUSIONS: Higher hospital caseload and vascular surgery specialization were independently associated with improved in-hospital survival after TBAD treatment. The findings support the centralization of complex aortic care and emphasize that both the procedural volume and dedicated vascular expertise contribute to optimal outcomes.

title: Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative Contemporary Benchmarks: Endovascular Abdominal Aortic Aneurysms.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative (SVS-VQI) Endovascular Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair (EVAR) registry represents the largest and most comprehensive prospectively maintained nonclaim-based dataset of endoluminal repairs in the North America. As part of the SVS-VQI benchmarking initiative, we sought to define national reference standards for patient selection, perioperative outcomes, and process-of-care metrics. METHODS: All EVAR procedures from 2011 to 2024 were included and stratified by indication as elective, symptomatic (intact and nonruptured), or ruptured. The primary end point was in-hospital mortality; secondary end points included in-hospital complications, adherence to SVS guideline-endorsed elective diameter treatment thresholds (men ≥ 5.5 cm; women ≥ 5.0 cm), discharge prescription of guideline-directed medical therapy, and 1-year follow-up compliance. Risk-adjusted observed-to-expected mortality ratios were derived from mixed-effects logistic regression models incorporating patient- and procedure-level covariates. Temporal trends were analyzed using linear and logistic regression across four periods: 2011 to 2013, 2014 to 2017, 2018 to 2021, and 2022 to 2024. RESULTS: Among 90,370 EVARs performed across >400 centers, 76,350 (85%) were elective, 8349 (9%) symptomatic-intact, and 5671 (6%) ruptured. Mean patient age was 73.5 ± 8.8 years, and 17,531 (19%) were women. Adoption of percutaneous femoral access increased markedly after 2014, exceeding 80% of all cases across the study period [overall rate, 81.1%; 95% confidence interval (CI), 80.8-81.4] and reaching a contemporary benchmark of 89.4% (95% CI, 89.1-89.8) in 2022 to 2024. In-hospital mortality was 0.5% (95% CI, 0.42-0.52) for elective, 2.2% (95% CI, 1.91-2.56) for symptomatic-intact, and 21.5% (95% CI, 20.4-22.6) for ruptured repairs. Over time, mortality declined from 0.6% in 2011 to 2013 to 0.4% in 2022 to 2024 (P = .02) for elective cases, from 2.3% to 1.8% (P = .14) for symptomatic-intact, and from 24.0% to 20.6% (P = .09) for ruptures. Composite in-hospital complication rates decreased significantly across all indications (P < .001). Among elective repairs, adherence to diameter-based guidelines improved modestly, with male noncompliance decreasing from 46% to 40% and female noncompliance declining from 23% to 21%. In 2024, 87% of patients were discharged on an antiplatelet agent, 83% on a statin, and 74% on both. By 2022, one-year clinical follow-up reached 79%, whereas imaging surveillance was reported in 51%. CONCLUSIONS: EVAR outcomes within the SVS-VQI demonstrate persistently low in-hospital mortality and improving perioperative morbidity over time. Despite these gains, opportunities remain to improve adherence to societally endorsed diameter treatment thresholds, optimal medical therapy, and post-EVAR imaging surveillance. These findings establish contemporary national benchmarks for EVAR performance and provide reference standards for center-level comparison and quality improvement within the SVS-VQI.

title: Non-contrast ultrashort echo time magnetic resonance imaging-guided staging predicts in vivo lower extremity endovascular procedural complexity.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Our understanding of plaque morphology and its relationship with procedural complexity and immediate technical failure (ITF) in percutaneous vascular intervention is poorly understood, particularly in tibial disease due to significant limitations of computed tomographic angiography, digital subtraction angiography, and duplex ultrasound imaging. Ultrashort echo time magnetic resonance imaging (UTE MRI) is a non-contrast, 3T MRI technique that can identify and differentiate plaque morphology and characteristics. The aim of this study was to create a UTE MRI-defined staging system to support clinicians in evaluating endovascular procedural complexity. METHODS: Patients scheduled for percutaneous vascular intervention underwent preoperative UTE MRI. Lesions were graded based on MRI-defined anatomical characteristics and plaque morphology on a four-scale staging system, where stage A was least severe and stage D was most severe. The primary outcome was the association of UTE stage with ITF and was evaluated using logistic regression. Secondary outcomes included associations between UTE stage and the number of wire/catheter escalations required during the procedure, and UTE stage and the number of treatment devices used. Transatlantic Intersociety Consensus (TASC) scoring was also evaluated and investigated for any influence on ITF. RESULTS: 2 2 A total of 47 patients with 90 arterial lesions were included. Stage D and stage C UTE MRI-defined disease strongly influenced ITF (odds ratio [OR], 114.3; 95% confidence interval [CI], 10.4-1257.5; P < .001 and OR, 21.0; 95% CI, 2.33-189.3; P = .007, respectively). Logistic regression identified that stage D disease was 99 times more likely to require catheter/wire escalations for crossing (OR, 0.01; 95% CI, 0.00-0.24; P = .004). The UTE MRI stage did not influence the number of treatment devices used (χ= 2.53; P = .47). Logistic regression showed that TASC score had no influence on ITF (χ= 2.13; P = .55). CONCLUSIONS: UTE MRI-defined staging is strongly associated with ITF, crossing time, and the need for crossing device escalation, whereas TASC staging had no influence on ITF. This study supports the notion that an understanding of plaque morphology and plaque characteristics is pivotal to procedural planning.

title: Contemporary assessment of great saphenous vein adequacy in patients with chronic limb-threatening limb ischemia.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: In patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), the Best Endovascular vs Best Surgical Therapy in Patients with CLTI (BEST-CLI) trial demonstrated a significant benefit of infrainguinal bypass with single-segment great saphenous vein (GSV). Given the rise of venous ablation and the lack of consistent vein mapping, the prevalence of adequate GSV is poorly defined in current patients with CLTI. Our goal was to assess the availability of adequate GSV in a contemporary CLTI population. METHODS: We conducted a single-center review of unique patients with CLTI (2016-2025) who had vein mapping before an open or endovascular intervention was performed. Patients with a history of prior open infrainguinal revascularizations were excluded. Duplex ultrasound reports were evaluated for GSV diameter. Vein diameter was assessed for a minimum of 2.5 mm throughout the thigh alone and 3 mm throughout the entire leg (thigh and calf). Ipsilateral and contralateral measurements were recorded. Patient and anatomical details were compared and stratified by available GSV. RESULTS: We identified 223 patients. The patients had a mean age of 68.6 years; 64.1% were male, 50.2% were of Black race, and 17.9% were of Hispanic ethnicity. The majority (69.1%) had diabetes mellitus, and 35% were currently smoking. Of these patients, 16.6% had a history of deep vein thrombosis, 18.4% had chronic venous insufficiency, and 0.9% had a prior GSV ablation; 29.1% had a prior ipsilateral infrainguinal endovascular intervention. With respect to duplex-based measurements, thigh GSV ≥2.5 mm alone was seen in 69.5% and 74% of the ipsilateral and either leg, respectively. Entire leg GSV ≥2.5 mm was observed in 42.9% and 46.6% of the ipsilateral and either leg, respectively. Thigh GSV ≥3 mm alone was seen in 58.7% and 64.6% of the ipsilateral and either leg, respectively. Entire leg GSV ≥3 mm was observed in 23.8% and 27.4% of the ipsilateral and either leg, respectively. Overall, 102 patients (45.7%) underwent femoropopliteal intervention, including 46 endovascular (20.6%) and 56 bypass (25.1%) procedures. Among patients undergoing femoropopliteal intervention, 153 (68.6%) had a thigh GSV diameter of ≥2.5 mm and 133 (59.8%) had a diameter of ≥3.0 mm. Male gender (odds ratio, 2.32; 95% confidence interval, 1.28-4.24; P = .006) and diabetes mellitus (odds ratio, 2.17; 95% confidence interval, 1.15-4.1; P = .02) were associated with >2.5 mm vein diameter on multivariable analysis. CONCLUSIONS: The majority of patients with CLTI had adequate thigh GSV, with a high percentage having adequate GSV throughout the entire leg. These findings suggest that a significant number of patients fit for revascularization could be candidates for a single-segment GSV bypass.

title: Evaluating growth patterns and rupture risk to determine the repair threshold for saccular abdominal aortic aneurysms.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Saccular abdominal aortic aneurysms (sAAAs) lack a specific International Classification of Diseases code, and data on clinical outcomes and size criteria for repair remain sparse. METHODS: We performed a large language model (LLM)-assisted term search to identify all consecutive patients with sAAA at a large multisystem hospital between April 1999 and August 2025. Patients with sAAA (group I) were compared with patients with fusiform AAA (fAAA; group II) using deidentified LLM data in the entire cohort. Clinical data including demographics, mode of detection, aneurysm size, and outcomes were retrospectively reviewed from a single center. The primary outcomes were rupture risk and aneurysm growth rate. RESULTS: The LLM accessed 1.3 billion clinical notes from 8 million patients over the study period and identified 298 patients (233 male; mean age, 75 ± 8 years) with sAAA and 42,971 with fAAA. The mean fAAA diameter was 4 ± 1 cm; no sAAA ruptures were observed at presentation or during long-term follow-up, regardless of aneurysm size. Clinical data validation was performed in 50 patients with sAAA (33 male; mean age, 81 ± 9 years; median initial maximum diameter, 4.1 cm [range, 3-6.2 cm]). The majority were detected incidentally. Thirty-two patients (64%) did not undergo repair. In this group, the initial mean sAAA diameter was 3.6 ± 1.0 cm. At a mean imaging follow-up of 57 months (average 3.5 scan/patient), the mean sAAA diameter increased to 4 ± 1.3 cm. The rate of aneurysm growth increased with increasing sAAA size (P = .03). Eighteen patients underwent repair (mean sAAA diameter, 5.4 ± 1.0 cm). Repair was performed because sAAAs were symptomatic in three patients, meeting traditional size criteria (5 cm in female and 5.5 cm in male patients) at the initial scan in two patients or on surveillance (mean, 32 months) in 12 patients. Repair was based on morphology alone in one asymptomatic patient. Procedures included open repair in four and endovascular repair in 14 patients; operative mortality was 2%. At a mean clinical follow-up of 80 months (median, 64 months), there was no additional aneurysm-related mortality. CONCLUSIONS: Rupture of AAA due to saccular morphology seems rare. Most sAAAs present incidentally and demonstrate slow growth rates when <5 cm in diameter. Intervention is safe and effective for sAAAs that meet the traditional criteria for repair for AAA. LLMs demonstrate potential utility in the identification of rare vascular pathologies that do not have defined International Classification of Diseases codes.
